name: Apple SHARP (Sharp Monocular View Synthesis)
domain: single photo -> 3D Gaussian splat scene (feed-forward, metric)
license: Weights: apple-amlr (Apple Machine Learning Research Model License — "exclusively for Research Purposes ... does not include any commercial exploitation, product development or use in any commercial product or service"); code: Apple sample-code license (GitHub spdx NOASSERTION / "Other"); Spark viewer: MIT (sparkjsdev/spark); SharpGlass: MIT; starkdmi MLX port: Apache-2.0 (code only, weights still amlr)
params: ~702M (not published; computed from the fp16 safetensors header of agg23/Sharp-mlx-f16: 702,305,169 params, 1,038 tensors — monodepth backbone 692.5M, feature model 7.8M, depth alignment 2.0M; cross-checks with the 2,809,738,232-byte fp32 .pt ÷ 4 bytes)
released: 2025-12-11 (arXiv 2512.10685 published; GitHub repo created 2025-12-12; HF apple/Sharp createdAt 2025-12-12; apple/ml-sharp last push 2025-12-19 — upstream dormant since, ecosystem active through 2026-08)
what: Regresses ~1.18M 3D Gaussians of the whole scene from one photograph in a single feed-forward pass (<1 s on a GPU, 1.9 s via Core ML on M4 Max, ~25 s in Chrome via the sharp-webgpu WGSL port). Output is a metric-scale .ply compatible with any 3DGS viewer; official repo runs prediction on MPS (video rendering needs CUDA).
why_cool: A flat photo becomes a scene you can lean into: parallax, occlusion reveal and depth-of-field emerge as the camera moves. Doing it entirely in the visitor's browser (drop image -> splat in ~25 s) is a demo people remember.
demo_idea: formless blog: a lab page where the visitor drops a photo, sharp-webgpu (Chrome/WebGPU) produces the 1.18M-splat scene client-side, then a scroll- or pointer-driven camera path plays it back; for the hero itself, pre-generate once with the Core ML build (1.9 s on M4 Max), convert to .spz and render with Spark so the landing image gains real parallax on mouse move.
mac_evidence: apple/ml-sharp README, section "Rendering trajectories (CUDA GPU only)": "While the gaussians prediction works for all CPU, CUDA, and MPS, rendering videos via the `--render` option currently requires a CUDA GPU." Issue #43 "Apple M4 sharp render error" confirms the only Mac failure is `sharp render` ("Rendering a checkpoint requires CUDA"); predict works. Third-party sharp-gui README platform table: "macOS Apple Silicon | MPS | 已验证 (verified)". requirements.txt pins nvidia-*/triton only under `platform_machine == 'x86_64' and sys_platform == 'linux'`; no flash-attn/xformers. Native MLX ports exist: starkdmi/ml_sharp_mlx (Python + Swift MLX, Apache-2.0, "Running entirely on Apple Silicon", Dec 2025) and mnmly/mlx-swift-ml-sharp (mlx-swift, "Numerically equivalent to the upstream Python pipeline", May 2026); HF agg23/Sharp-mlx-f16 ships sharp_fp16.safetensors (1.4 GB). Browser path also exists but is left out of the feasibility call as unverified on Safari: bring-shrubbery/ml-sharp-web (295 stars, pushed 2026-07-01, live at ml-sharp-web.vercel.app) runs the predictor in-browser with onnxruntime-web 1.24.2, `executionProviders: ['webgpu', 'wasm']` fallback, ~2.4 GB ONNX sidecar. No published seconds-per-image on any M-series chip anywhere (README, issues #27/#43/#79, MLX port READMEs); "<1 s" is the paper's GPU claim only.
notes: All candidate claims check out. Evidence: GitHub apple/ml-sharp 8,879 stars; HF apple/Sharp 2,134 downloads / 407 likes, not gated, files = sharp_2572gikvuh.pt (2.81 GB) + README + LICENSE; no safetensors/gguf on the official repo. No mlx-community port (author search returns 0), but community MLX weights exist (agg23/Sharp-mlx-f16) plus two MLX code ports; ONNX exports exist on HF (pearsonkyle/Sharp-onnx fp16, Olsc/sharp-onnx-int8, mxtx0123/ml-sharp-onnx) and even a Qualcomm QNN port (2026-08). Spark: 3,582 stars, v2.1.0 released 2026-05-18, README lists .PLY/.SPZ/.SPLAT/.KSPLAT/.SOG input and "98%+ WebGL2 support" — fits the formless ogl/WebGL page. Ecosystem is very much alive in 2026: ml-sharp-web (in-browser ONNX WebGPU, Jul 2026), ComfyUI-Sharp 361 stars (Aug 2026), sharp-gui 190 stars Spark-based viewer (Aug 2026), cullenwebber/three-ml-sharp 123 stars (SHARP → three.js GPGPU particles, Feb 2026). Corrections to candidate: SharpGlass README says weights are "approx. 1.2GB" — actual checkpoint is 2.8 GB. gsplat (CUDA rasterizer) is a hard pip dependency but only used by --render; starkdmi/gsplat-mps (AGPL-3.0) exists if MPS video rendering is wanted. Model license is enforced on all derivatives (ONNX/MLX conversions inherit amlr), so the beu commercial exclusion stands; the lab/blog demo is fine. Upgrade path for extra 간지: the ml-sharp-web approach shows the 700M predictor itself can run in-page under WebGPU (Chrome verified by that project; Safari 26 untested, 2.4 GB download), so a "drop a photo, orbit it" demo entirely client-side is plausible but should be treated as a stretch goal after the Mac-generated .ply + Spark embed.

name: BiRefNet dynamic 1024 (browser cutout / matting)
domain: background removal & alpha matting, client-side
license: MIT
params: 220.7M (HF safetensors total 220,700,242 F16 for ZhengPeng7/BiRefNet and BiRefNet_dynamic-matting); ONNX: dynamic-1024 fp32 972.5 MB / fp16 489.8 MB, BiRefNet_lite fp16 114.5 MB, BEN2 fp16 219.1 MB (BEN2 param count not exposed by HF metadata)
released: Dynamic-1024 ONNX: HF createdAt 2026-09-01 (last commit 2026-09-04). BiRefNet_dynamic-matting: HF 2025-07-11. Base BiRefNet HF weights 2024-07-12; paper arXiv 2401.03407 (Jan 2024); GitHub repo created 2022-08-17, last push 2026-09-02, 4,165 stars.
what: BiRefNet (221M params, MIT) is the high-resolution dichotomous segmentation model that quietly replaced rembg; a new dynamic-resolution 1024x1024 ONNX build landed on 2026-09-01 in onnx-community and runs through Transformers.js's image-segmentation pipeline (fp16 490 MB; BiRefNet_lite fp16 115 MB, or BEN2 fp16 219 MB, MIT, as lighter alternatives). The BiRefNet_dynamic-matting checkpoint (Jul 2025) adds soft alpha for hair/glass edges.
why_cool: Drop a phone photo of a glossy bottle and get a hair-accurate, glass-edge-aware cutout in a second or two with zero upload — the 'text behind video' cinematic effect that went viral in Feb 2026 is the same trick applied per frame.
demo_idea: beu: browser-only compositor — cutout the container, drop it on studio backdrops with a synthetic contact shadow, then overlay the label design; nothing leaves the customer's machine, which is a selling point. Blog: hero title rendered 'behind' the visitor's own webcam silhouette (BEN2 219 MB) in the ogl scene.
mac_evidence: In-browser path is confirmed for the family: HF space webml-community/text-behind-video (static, created 2026-02-24, 52 likes) src/App.tsx calls pipeline("background-removal", "onnx-community/BEN2-ONNX", { device: "webgpu" }) with @huggingface/transformers ^4.0.0-next.4; onnx-community/BiRefNet_lite-ONNX (transformers.js, fp16 114.5 MB) has 5,692 downloads. The new onnx-community/BiRefNet_dynamic-1024x1024-ONNX (transformers.js library tag, MIT, onnx/model_fp16.onnx 489.8 MB) exists but is 4 days old with 39 downloads / 0 likes, uploaded by user CORTON (not HF staff); its card example uses AutoModel with dtype 'fp32' and no device:'webgpu' shown, so the 490 MB fp16 WebGPU path is unproven. Native Apple Silicon also exists: mlx-community/BiRefNet-fp16 and mlx-community/BiRefNet_HR-matting-fp16 (2026-06-22, MLX safetensors, IoU 0.9905 parity, loaded via xocialize/mlx-birefnet-swift); CoreML ports metaclass/birefnet-lite-coreml (2026-08-08) and avencera/birefnet-coreml-gpu (2026-08-26). GitHub README has no MLX/CoreML/mps mention; examples use .to('cuda') but no hard CUDA-only kernel requirement (Sep 2025 switched Swin attention to PyTorch SDPA; inference 3.5 GB fp16 at 1024).
notes: Verified all six source URLs resolve and weights are public/ungated. Corrections to the candidate text: (1) 'dynamic' refers to the BiRefNet_dynamic checkpoint trained on 256x256-2304x2304 inputs, not a dynamic-shape ONNX graph - the ONNX repo's preprocessor_config.json pins size 1024x1024 and the repo name says so; (2) the dynamic-1024 ONNX is a community upload (CORTON), not from Xenova, and there is no public demo running it in a browser yet - the viral text-behind-video space uses BEN2-ONNX, not BiRefNet; (3) the matting checkpoint (BiRefNet_dynamic-matting) has no ONNX in onnx-community; community ONNX ports exist (emrikol/birefnet-matting-onnx 2026-06-30, PinkPixel/birefnet-hr-matting-onnx 2026-09-07) but were not inspected. 'Went viral in Feb 2026' is not verifiable from metadata (space created 2026-02-24, 52 likes). For beu the safest shipping pick today is BEN2-ONNX (219 MB fp16, WebGPU proven) or BiRefNet_lite-ONNX (115 MB); the 490 MB dynamic-1024 build should be benchmarked in Safari 26/Chrome WebGPU before committing. Official GitHub release v1 (2024-05-13) also hosts .pth and .onnx for all variants, including BiRefNet_dynamic-matting-epoch_159.pth.

name: Bonsai-Image ternary 4B (text-to-image on WebGPU / MLX)
domain: generative visuals reacting to the visitor, in-browser diffusion
license: Apache-2.0 (HF cardData.license on the model repo; GitHub PrismML-Eng/Bonsai-Image-Demo SPDX Apache-2.0). The required mflux fork PrismML-Eng/mflux-prism is MIT.
params: ~4.0B transformer trunk (FLUX.2 Klein 4B MMDiT, 25 blocks) + Qwen3-4B text encoder at 4-bit; HF API does not report a safetensors param count. On-disk (HF tree): transformer 1,425,271,472 B (1.43 GB MLX pack; the 1.21 GB figure is the model-level representation), text encoder 2,263,022,529 B, VAE 168,120,878 B; manifest.json total_bytes 3,888,274,639.
released: 2026-05-21 (HF createdAt of the ternary mlx-2bit repo; binary sibling 2026-05-18; GitHub demo repo created 2026-05-05; card citation "May 2026"). Model repo lastModified 2026-06-01; demo repo pushed 2026-09-08 (533 stars).
what: PrismML's Bonsai-Image (May 2026) is a ternary {-1,0,+1} 1.58-bit quantization of a FLUX.2-Klein-4B-class MMDiT: the 4B transformer shrinks from 7.75 GB fp16 to 1.21 GB, generates 1024x1024 in 4 FlowMatch-Euler steps without CFG, and ships as MLX 2-bit for mflux (~6 s per 1024² image on an M4 Pro, 3.88 GB total payload with 4-bit text encoder + VAE), a LiteRT build, and a Hugging Face WebGPU space that generates entirely in the browser. Note: it is a FLUX.2 Klein derivative, so it overlaps the already-covered Klein lineage — the new angle is the browser/ternary runtime.
why_cool: State-of-the-art-looking 1024² images generated by the visitor's own GPU, in a tab, with no API key — the first time a 4B diffusion model has been a realistic client-side payload.
demo_idea: formless 'living hero': the page composes a prompt from visitor context (local time, scroll depth, cursor-sampled palette from the WebGL field) and, behind a one-click 3.9 GB opt-in, renders a unique hero image on WebGPU; fall back to mflux-generated variants on the Mac for visitors who decline. Lab: benchmark ternary-4B in mflux on the M4 Max (steps, seconds, memory) vs the WebGPU space in Safari 26 and Chrome.
mac_evidence: HF card (prism-ml/bonsai-image-ternary-4B-mlx-2bit, tags mlx/apple-silicon): "MLX-native 2-bit format for Apple Silicon", "Mac M4 Pro (48 GB), 4 steps: 512x512 5.78 s/image; 1024x1024 24.26 s/image (6.06 s/step)", "mean-active memory pressure at 1024² is 2.38 GB"; demo setup.sh: "mflux requires Apple Silicon (arm64)". WebGPU space webml-community/bonsai-image-webgpu (static SDK, RUNNING, 338 likes, lastModified 2026-05-29) UI text: "All inference happens in your browser via WebGPU. No server calls" / "Research software, primarily tested on Apple M4 Max and M5 Max ... On Chrome/Edge, enable chrome://flags/#enable-unsafe-webgpu for best performance" / ternary variant "3.3 GB". Bundle inspection: bespoke WGSL runtime (63 @compute kernels, label "webgpu-ml-runtime") fetching the same HF safetensors (transformer-packed-mflux/, text_encoder-mlx-4bit/, vae/); requiredFeatures = only those the adapter has among [shader-f16, subgroups, chromium-experimental-subgroup-matrix] with float32 fallback, so Safari is not excluded by code, but Safari 26 is not documented or tested by the authors. Caveat: the space hard-requires a HuggingFace access token ("Token required." — Bearer validated against api/models and attached to all HF fetches) even though the repo is not gated.
notes: Verified: URL resolves (HTTP 200, public, not gated, 95 likes, 905 downloads), safetensors weights present, whitepaper PDF (3.7 MB) in demo repo, WebGPU space live. Corrections to the candidate text: (1) "~6 s per 1024² on M4 Pro" is wrong — the card's ~6 s is per 512²; 1024² is 24.26 s (6.06 s/step) on M4 Pro, so expect roughly 12-20 s on the M4 Max, not 6. (2) "ships as MLX 2-bit for mflux" overstates it: stock mflux-community/mflux (v0.19.1, 2026-08-26) has zero code hits for "bonsai"; the only Mac path is the fork PrismML-Eng/mflux-prism (MIT, 5 stars, single commit "Bonsai Image v1 — klein_fast transformer backend" on top of mflux 0.17.5, untouched since 2026-05-11) vendored by Bonsai-Image-Demo/setup.sh together with PrismML-Eng/image-studio (FastAPI + Next.js). Community GGUF conversions exist (Green-Sky, Aatricks) but are not MLX. (3) No mlx-community port (search returns 0; unneeded, the official repo is MLX-native) and no ONNX/Transformers.js port of Bonsai-Image (onnx-community only has the Bonsai LLMs) — the browser path is a custom WebGPU runtime, not Transformers.js v4/ORT-Web, and its source is not published anywhere I could find: the space ships only a 912 KB minified bundle (assets/index-Bf-HmMxp.js) with no GitHub/npm reference; third parties patch the bundle directly (ArtyomITA/bonsai-webgpu-tiled-vae-fix). Embedding in formless means vendoring that minified bundle. (4) The space requires a personal HF token, so a public "one-click opt-in" needs self-hosted weights (Apache-2.0 permits redistribution) plus swapping the fetch URLs; the UI reports 3.3 GB but the three safetensors sum to 3.86 GB. (5) Safari 26 is unverified — authors only mention Chrome/Edge flag and testing on M4 Max/M5 Max; the code requests features optionally with float32 fallback, and weights are cached in IndexedDB. (6) LiteRT build (litert-community, 2026-07-29, updated 2026-09-05) is real but Mac Metal path is fp32 at ~22 GB RAM with a 40 s compile, output fixed 512² — not the right Mac path. (7) Official Gradio space prism-ml/Bonsai-Image-Demo is PAUSED (L4). Overlap with the already-covered FLUX.2 Klein lineage is confirmed (diffusers class Flux2KleinPipeline, base FLUX.2 Klein 4B); the genuinely new angle is only the ternary in-browser runtime. Quality per card: GenEval 0.723 vs Klein 4B 0.819.

name: DINOv3 ViT-S/16 in the browser (onnx-community + Transformers.js)
domain: image dedup / retrieval with a CLIP successor; distilled backbone
license: DINOv3 License (Meta custom). HF cardData: license=other, license_name=dinov3-license, license_link=https://ai.meta.com/resources/models-and-libraries/dinov3-license. GitHub facebookresearch/dinov3 SPDX=NOASSERTION ("Other"). Demo space webml-community/dinov3-web is apache-2.0.
params: 21,596,544 (21.6M, F32) per HF safetensors metadata on base facebook/dinov3-vits16-pretrain-lvd1689m; ONNX sizes: fp32 86.3MB, int8 (model_quantized) 21.8MB, q4 14.7MB. No fp16/q4f16 build for ViT-S/16.
released: 2025-08 (HF base model createdAt 2025-08-05; GitHub repo created 2025-08-07; paper arXiv 2508.10104; ONNX repo createdAt 2025-08-14; Transformers.js support in v3.7.2 on 2025-08-15). Still actively maintained: GitHub last push 2026-07-15 (CHMv2 2026-03-10, metadata-guided FINO branch 2026-06-12); CHMv2 DPT-head ONNX export 2026-03-17.
what: Meta's self-supervised vision backbone (7B teacher trained on 1.7B images, distilled to ViT-S/16 = 21.6M params) producing dense patch features and a global embedding; onnx-community ships ViT-S/S+/B/L and ConvNeXt variants for Transformers.js, plus a 2026-03 DPT depth head export. Cosine similarity of CLS/pooled embeddings gives near-duplicate detection and retrieval with no training.
why_cool: The PCA feature heatmap that shows the model 'seeing' object parts, and a grid where near-duplicates cluster instantly, all computed client-side on 200 dropped images in a few seconds, reads as magic to a visitor and is the exact Xenova demo (webml-community/dinov3-web, 160 likes) but you own it.
demo_idea: Blog: a WebGPU page where the visitor drops a folder of photos; the page embeds each with DINOv3-ViT-S (q4/fp16 ONNX), draws the PCA feature map on hover, and collapses near-duplicates (cosine > 0.9) into stacks with a slider for the threshold. beu: run the same embedding over the product-shot library to dedupe renders and to do 'find shots with this bottle silhouette' retrieval; combine with the depth-head ONNX (dinov3-vitl16-chmv2-dpt-head-ONNX) for a relief/normal-map look on bottle images in the formless WebGL hero.
mac_evidence: ONNX repo is public and ungated (gated=False; anonymous GET of onnx/model_q4.onnx returns HTTP 200), library_name=transformers.js, config.json carries transformers.js_config. The reference demo webml-community/dinov3-web (static SDK, runtime RUNNING, 160 likes) imports @huggingface/transformers@3.7.2 and does `const device = navigator.gpu ? "webgpu" : "wasm"; const dtype = webgpu ? "q4" : "q8"` then `pipeline("image-feature-extraction", MODEL_ID, {device, dtype})`, so it runs in WebGPU or WASM with a 14.7MB q4 model. Native Apple Silicon also covered: mlx-vision/vit_small_patch16_224.dinov3-mlxim, vit_small_plus_patch16_224.dinov3-mlxim, vit_base_patch16_224.dinov3-mlxim (mlx-image, created 2026-03-11..13) and SharpAI CoreML builds of ViT-S/B at 224-560px (2025-10/11). No mlx-community port. GitHub README: "Installing PyTorch with CUDA support is strongly recommended" but PyTorch is the only required dependency; CUDA autocast appears only in the 7B adapter examples, and multi-H100 requirements apply only to pretraining.
notes: Verified: URL resolves; weights present in ONNX; GitHub 11,333 stars; base PyTorch weights facebook/dinov3-vits16-pretrain-lvd1689m are gated=manual (license click-through) but the ONNX mirror is not gated so browser fetches work anonymously. onnx-community also ships vits16plus, vitb16, vitl16 (lvd1689m + sat493m), vith16plus, convnext tiny/small/base/large, and MHA/MHA-scores variants of vits16. Latest Transformers.js is 4.2.0 (2026-04-23). Space pawlo2013/Dinov3_Image_Retrieval exists (gradio, SLEEPING, 3 likes, created 2025-12). x.com source not fetched/verified. Two corrections to the candidate text: (1) dinov3-web does NOT draw a PCA feature map; it computes patch-token L2-normalized features (pooling:"none", skipping CLS + 4 register tokens) and a patch-vs-patch cosine similarity matrix via matmul, then draws a similarity heatmap for the hovered patch. A PCA-to-RGB map would be your own addition (cheap: 3-component PCA over 384-dim patch vectors). (2) onnx-community/dinov3-vitl16-chmv2-dpt-head-ONNX is CHMv2 = "Improvements in Global Canopy Height Mapping using DINOv3" (arXiv 2603.06382), a tree-canopy-height regressor for satellite/aerial imagery on a ViT-L backbone (fp32 1.35GB, fp16 674MB, q4 305MB, q4f16 232MB). It is not a general monocular depth model, so the "relief/normal map on bottle images" idea is a misuse; use Depth Anything v2 small ONNX or similar for that instead. The ViT-S/16 backbone itself has no fp16 export, only fp32/q8/q4, so the "q4/fp16" phrasing should read "q4 (WebGPU) / q8 (WASM)". Dedup/retrieval via CLS or mean-pooled embeddings needs no training and is well supported by the image-feature-extraction pipeline.

name: Depth Anything 3 Small (ByteDance Seed) in the browser
domain: single image -> geometry (depth/point map) in-browser; 2.5D for web pages
license: Apache-2.0 (GitHub spdx_id; HF cardData apache-2.0 on depth-anything/DA3-SMALL, DA3-BASE, DA3METRIC-LARGE and on both ONNX exports). README model table: DA3-LARGE, DA3-GIANT, DA3NESTED-GIANT-LARGE and their -1.1 refreshes are CC BY-NC 4.0.
params: DA3-SMALL: 34,299,463 params (HF safetensors F32 total; README lists 0.08B). DA3-BASE 0.12B, DA3-LARGE/DA3METRIC-LARGE 0.35B, DA3-GIANT 1.15B, NESTED 1.40B. Only Large/Giant got the -1.1 retrain (2025-12-11); Small/Base have a single Nov-2025 checkpoint.
released: 2025-11-13 (HF DA3-SMALL createdAt 2025-11-13; arXiv 2511.10647 v1 2025-11-13; GitHub repo created 2025-11-12, README news '14-11-2025: paper, code and models released'). ONNX export by onnx-community 2025-11-14. Repo still active: commits 2026-07-13/15/27 (backend/Gradio updates), latest issue activity 2026-09-02. No GitHub releases or tags.
what: DA3 is the any-view geometry model (Nov 2025, v1.1 Dec 2025, repo still active Jul 2026) that predicts consistent depth, poses and (Giant) Gaussians from 1..N images; the Small (0.08B) and Base (0.12B) variants are Apache-2.0 and have onnx-community ONNX exports for ONNX Runtime Web / Transformers.js, so single-image depth runs client-side on WebGPU in Safari 26 and Chrome.
why_cool: The page itself computes a depth map of any image in well under a second and turns it into a displaced, parallaxing 3D surface that follows the cursor; no server, works on phones, and the model is 34 MB.
demo_idea: formless blog: run onnx-community/depth-anything-v3-small via ONNX Runtime Web (WebGPU EP, WASM fallback) on the hero image, feed the depth texture to the existing ogl scene as a displaced plane with pointer parallax and depth-based blur, and let the reader drop their own photo to see it lifted into 2.5D; fall back to depth-anything-v2-small if the DA3 export needs a custom pre/post pipeline in Transformers.js.
mac_evidence: (1) ONNX export exists and runs: onnx-community/depth-anything-v3-small ships onnx/model.onnx (0.6 MB graph) + model.onnx_data (104.7 MB fp32), config.json = {"model_type":"depth_anything","transformers.js_config":{"dtype":"fp32","use_external_data_format":true}}, NO preprocessor_config.json. Graph (opset 18, exported with torch 2.9.1) input pixel_values [batch_size, num_images, 3, height, width]; outputs predicted_depth [B,N,H,W], confidence, extrinsics [B,N,3,4], intrinsics [B,N,3,3]. I downloaded it and ran it on this Mac with onnxruntime 1.29.0 CPU EP: 305 ms at 392x294, outputs (1,1,294,392); feeding a 4-D tensor fails with 'Invalid rank for input: pixel_values Got: 4 Expected: 5'. (2) Live browser deployment: en970/depth-anything-v3-small-onnx (2026-08-11, base_model onnx-community/depth-anything-v3-small): 'The upstream repository ships float32 only, at 105 MB ... This export is 28.9 MB' (model_quantized.onnx q8 + model_fp16.onnx 53 MB); measured 8-bit 90-113 ms at 322 px, Pearson r 0.990-0.998 vs fp32. It is wired into en970/depth-realtime (pushed 2026-08-23, live at en970.github.io/depth-realtime, '@huggingface/transformers': '4.2.0', AutoModelForDepthEstimation, WebGPU EP with WASM q8 fallback) as `v3: { id: "en970/depth-anything-v3-small-onnx", rank5: true, invert: true }`, selectable via #model=v3; author notes 'V3 also takes a rank-5 input, with a leading image count', 'V3 exponentiates log depth in its head, so it emits depth directly and larger is farther', and 'measured in the browser it runs at DA2's speed, not faster'. (3) ORT-web WebGPU operator table covers every op in the DA3 graph (Einsum, ScatterND, LayerNormalization, Tan, ConvTranspose, Resize, Range, Cos/Sin, Erf, Gemm, Where...) except ConstantOfShape (falls back to CPU; Shape/Reshape are 'no GPU kernel' anyway). (4) Native fallback also proven: PR #26 'Simple fix for MPS support' merged 2025-11-17 ('Verified on macOS with MPS that the model runs end-to-end'); PR #123 'perf(mps): disable GPU preprocessing on Apple Silicon' merged; xformers is listed in pyproject dependencies but src/depth_anything_3/model/dinov2/layers/swiglu_ffn.py guards it ('try: from xformers.ops import SwiGLU ... except ImportError: SwiGLU = SwiGLUFFN') and attention.py uses F.scaled_dot_product_attention. CoreML port mlboydaisuke/Depth-Anything-3-Small-CoreML (2026-08-03, 44 MB, 'on-device inference on iPhone, iPad and Mac', iOS 17+) and LiteRT port litert-community/Depth-Anything-3-Small (2026-06-25, FP16 55 MB). No mlx-community DA3 port (mlx-community only has Video-Depth-Anything-*-MLX, 2026-09-01). No hard CUDA/VRAM requirement for the Small/Base models.
notes: Corrections to the candidate: (a) '34 MB' is wrong for the onnx-community export, which is 105 MB fp32 with no fp16/q8 variants (an 'Upload model_fp16.onnx' PR from 2025-11-17 is still open); the 28.9 MB q8 / 53 MB fp16 files live in en970/depth-anything-v3-small-onnx (Aug 2026). 34M is the parameter count. (b) Transformers.js pipeline('depth-estimation') will NOT work out of the box: the pipeline feeds a rank-4 pixel_values from a processor, the repo has no preprocessor_config.json, the graph demands rank 5, and Transformers.js 4.2.0 (2026-04-23) has no DA3-specific class (DepthAnythingForDepthEstimation is an empty subclass). Working recipe (from depth-realtime): resize to a multiple of 14, ImageNet-normalize to NCHW, unsqueeze to [1,1,3,H,W], call AutoModelForDepthEstimation directly or raw onnxruntime-web, then invert predicted_depth (DA3 outputs depth, large = far, unlike DA v2's inverse depth). (c) No official ONNX from ByteDance (issue #141 open; community scripts MSch8791/da3_onnx, MapMindAI). (d) Small/Base never got the -1.1 retrain, so the Nov-2025 ONNX export is the current checkpoint. (e) The third-party browser measurement says DA3-Small runs at DA2-Small speed, not faster; its advantage is far-field detail ('179 distinct levels against V2's 10'). Demo bonus: the export also emits per-image intrinsics (3x3) and extrinsics, so the ogl scene can unproject to a real point cloud instead of only displacing a plane. Safari 26 WebGPU support was not verified from these sources; depth-realtime targets Safari/Chrome and says WebGPU is unavailable on iOS 18-25.

params: Candidate says 0.08B. Reality: DA3-SMALL model card says 0.08B, but HF safetensors metadata reports 34,299,463 params (F32), and the onnx-community ONNX graph declares 26,179,702 initializer elements (104.7 MB model.onnx_data fp32 + 640 KB graph). ONNX export by Xenova 2025-11-14/15, untouched since. GitHub last push 2026-07-27, 6,300 stars. mlx-community Video-Depth-Anything MLX ports 2026-09-01; DA3Mono-LARGE-MLX 2026-08-21.
what: DA3 (ICLR 2026) predicts depth and camera rays from one or many views; the 80M DA3-Small mono checkpoint is exported by onnx-community with model_type 'depth_anything' and a transformers.js_config, so it loads with the standard Transformers.js depth-estimation pipeline (~105 MB fp32, fp16 also present). Video-Depth-Anything Small/Base/Large got MLX ports in Sept 2026 for offline video.

demo_idea: formless blog hero: run the Transformers.js depth-estimation pipeline on the generative hero's current frame (or a dropped photo), upload the depth map as an ogl texture, and displace a plane mesh so the cover parallaxes with the mouse and 'breathes' with scroll; this fits the existing LivingTitle push/lift/lean rules. Stretch: webcam mode at ~10 fps for a self-portrait relief. beu: depth map of a product shot gives the cylinder axis and curvature for wrapping label art. For video, mlx-community/Video-Depth-Anything-Small-MLX on the Mac produces temporally consistent depth for a hero loop.
mac_evidence: Downgraded from 'browser' because the key browser claim does not hold as stated. (1) Transformers.js 4.2.0 (latest, 2026-04-23) registry maps 'depth_anything' -> DepthAnythingForDepthEstimation, a bare PreTrainedModel with no DA3 handling; AutoProcessor.from_pretrained calls getModelJSON(..., 'preprocessor_config.json', true) i.e. fatal, and the onnx-community repo has NO preprocessor_config.json (siblings: .gitattributes, README.md, config.json, onnx/model.onnx, onnx/model.onnx_data). So pipeline('depth-estimation', 'onnx-community/depth-anything-v3-small') throws at processor load. (2) Inspecting onnx/model.onnx (opset 18, producer pytorch 2.9.1): input pixel_values is 5-D [batch_size, num_images, 3, height, width]; outputs predicted_depth [B,N,H,W], confidence, extrinsics [B,N,3,4], intrinsics (ScatterND-produced). This is the any-view model with camera heads, not a 4-D mono DPT export; the standard pipeline's 4-D tensor would be rank-mismatched. No transformers.js issue/PR mentions Depth Anything 3. (3) No verified in-browser DA3 demo found: en970/depth-anything-v3-small-onnx (2026-08-11, Apache-2.0, fp16 + 8-bit 28.9 MB, 90-218 ms at 322 px) was 'produced for' the browser viewer en970/depth-realtime, but that live site ships onnx-community/depth-anything-v2-small (WebGPU via Transformers.js 4.2.0, 47-74 ms/inference on Apple Silicon, Safari 26+ supported) — DA3 was not adopted. So browser is plausible via raw onnxruntime-web with custom pre/post-processing but unproven. Mac-native IS supported: ONNX (105 MB fp32 / 29 MB q8) runs on ORT CPU/CoreML; CoreML ports exist (sdkv2/DepthAnythingV3Mono-CoreML 2026-06, mrgnw/depth-anything-v3-coreml 2026-07); PyTorch MPS float64 fix PR #26 merged 2025-11-17; mlx-community/DA3Mono-LARGE-MLX (334M, validated Pearson r 0.9999998 vs PyTorch) and Video-Depth-Anything-{Small,Base,Large}-MLX exist and mlx-vlm v0.7.0 (2026-09-07) ships mlx_vlm/models/video_depth_anything. Caveats: reference repo install pins xformers and the example hardcodes cuda; PRs #233 (drop xformers for macOS), #262 (fix(mac) inference/training) and #237 (MLX conversion of DA3) are all still open/unmerged; no MLX port of the Apache DA3-SMALL/BASE exists.
notes: URL resolves and weights exist, but several candidate claims are wrong. (a) 'fp16 also present' is false for the onnx-community repo: only fp32 model.onnx + model.onnx_data; HF PR #2 'Upload model_fp16.onnx' (rblack21, 2025-11-17) is still open/unmerged. fp16 and q8 exist only in the third-party derivative en970/depth-anything-v3-small-onnx (2026-08-11, Apache-2.0). (b) 'loads with the standard Transformers.js depth-estimation pipeline' is false as of Transformers.js 4.2.0: no preprocessor_config.json in the repo (fatal load), and the graph takes 5-D input and returns depth+confidence+extrinsics+intrinsics. A demo needs a hand-written processor (resize to multiples of 14, ImageNet normalize, unsqueeze to [1,1,3,H,W]) and either a direct onnxruntime-web session or Transformers.js with a custom processor; WebGPU EP coverage of ScatterND etc. is unverified. The repo README is empty and has 235 downloads — an experimental Xenova export, never revisited. (c) '80M params' comes from the model card; safetensors metadata says 34.3M and the ONNX graph 26.2M. (d) 'ICLR 2026' not found in the README, project page, or arXiv abs (no Comments field); web search budget was exhausted so venue is unverified. (e) Video-Depth-Anything MLX ports are confirmed (mlx-community, 2026-09-01, via mlx-vlm v0.7.0) but they are ports of the Jan-2025 Video-Depth-Anything (CVPR 2025), not DA3; the Small MLX card is mislabeled cc-by-nc-4.0 (upstream says Small is Apache-2.0). (f) Upstream issue #182 (open) confirms DA3 is not in HF transformers either. Demo implication: the cheapest proven route for the formless hero on WebGPU today is still onnx-community/depth-anything-v2-small via the standard pipeline (en970/depth-realtime shows Safari 26/Chrome at 10-20 fps); DA3-small in-browser is a small porting project, not a drop-in. Official Gradio Space depth-anything/depth-anything-3 exists. Sources checked: HF API for onnx-community/depth-anything-v3-small (+commits, discussions, tree), depth-anything/DA3-SMALL/BASE/MONO-LARGE/METRIC-LARGE, mlx-community/*Depth-Anything*, en970/*, ByteDance-Seed/Depth-Anything-3 (README, license, issues #26 #182 #233 #237 #262), huggingface/transformers.js (registry.js, processing_auto.js, modeling_depth_anything.js, release 4.2.0), Blaizzy/mlx-vlm (video_depth_anything module, v0.7.0), DepthAnything/Video-Depth-Anything README, en970/depth-realtime README + package.json, arXiv 2511.10647.

(2) The candidate's source https://huggingface.co/blog/transformersjs-v4 does not mention EdgeTAM at all (0 hits) — drop it; the real evidence is the Transformers.js README + registry.js. (1) Version mismatch: the official Space pins @huggingface/transformers ^3.7.2, not v4; v4 support exists in source (registry.js) but Apple has not demonstrated it — test on v4.2.0 yourself, and note Safari 26 WebGPU is asserted by the candidate, not by any source I checked. (2) Download weight: the Space's dtype config is ~1.09 GB (vision_encoder_q4.onnx is 505 MB, identical to fp32 because q4 does not touch conv weights; vision_encoder_q4f16 is 253 MB, int8 223 MB; decoder q4 317 MB; embed fp16 272 MB). A blog hero pulling 1 GB is a real UX cost; SmolVLM2-256M q4 config is ~208 MB. (3) Staleness: apple/ml-fastvlm has 7,415 stars but a single commit (2025-05-05), 0 releases, 57 open issues; ONNX repo 109 likes, Space 447 likes (matches claim). No FastVLM-2; all 2026 activity is community (dbaek111 fastvlm-0.5b-mlx-q4/q8/fp16 2026-07-08; SpacemiT/FastVLM-0.5B 2026-08-18; hf-tiny-v2 test repos 2026-08-13) plus Transformers.js v4 keeping the model type registered. what: Two small models that already ship as Transformers.js-ready ONNX: onnx-community/BiRefNet_dynamic-1024x1024-ONNX (MIT, published Sept 2026) for high-res product matting with dynamic input size, and onnx-community/depth-anything-v3-small (Apache-2.0, 34M params, ByteDance DA3) for monocular depth. It is the 'small ML in the page' idea the blog hero was missing, and it is the cheapest realistic label mockup beu can offer.
demo_idea: formless blog page + beu prototype: Transformers.js v4 pipeline('image-segmentation', BiRefNet_dynamic) to cut the bottle, pipeline('depth-estimation', depth-anything-v3-small) for depth, then an ogl fragment shader that (1) builds normals from depth gradients, (2) samples the user's label PNG through depth-displaced cylindrical UVs so it hugs the bottle, (3) adds a Blinn-Phong light bound to pointer position plus an HDR-ish rim. Measure Safari 26 vs Chrome WebGPU load and per-frame times for the lab repo.
mac_evidence: Both halves run in Transformers.js on WebGPU, but not via the pipeline() calls the candidate describes. (1) BiRefNet: HF repo has library_name transformers.js, preprocessor_config.json, and a README snippet using AutoModel/AutoProcessor with input `input_image`; weights are onnx/model.onnx 972.5 MB fp32 and onnx/model_fp16.onnx 489.8 MB (no q8/q4). Community browser code (pix3dev/pix3 bg-removal.worker.ts) loads onnx-community/BiRefNet-ONNX with `device:'webgpu', dtype:'fp16'` and fp32 fallback, and states: "static 1024x1024 input ... OOMs the 32-bit WASM heap. It therefore needs WebGPU". (2) DA3-small: onnx-community repo is fp32 only (model.onnx 0.6 MB + model.onnx_data 104.7 MB), README contains only the license line, no preprocessor_config.json (404), no transformers.js tag. Inspected graph: opset 18, input `pixel_values [batch_size, num_images, 3, height, width]` (rank 5), outputs predicted_depth/confidence/extrinsics/intrinsics. Transformers.js registry maps `depth_anything` to DepthAnythingForDepthEstimation only (0 hits for DepthAnything3/depth_anything_3), so pipeline('depth-estimation') will not work as-is. Proven browser route: en970/depth-realtime (MIT, Aug 2026) loads `en970/depth-anything-v3-small-onnx` (fp16 53.0 MB, q8 28.9 MB, q8 Pearson r 0.990-0.998 vs fp32) with AutoModelForDepthEstimation.from_pretrained({device:'webgpu'}), hand-builds a `[1,1,3,H,W]` tensor with ImageNet mean/std, and inverts output ("Depth: large-is-far, so it must be flipped"). The 2B Qwen3-VL-based model beats the 72B Qwen2.5-VL on captioning benchmarks; CapRL++ (2026-06) extended the recipe to video (CapRL-Video-4B). Apache-2.0 weights, GGUF builds, and standard qwen3_vl architecture so it loads in mlx-vlm.
why_cool: A 2B model writing paragraph-length, verifiably accurate captions (charts, infographics, product labels) at laptop speed is the piece that turns a folder of images into a training set; showing the caption next to the 72B baseline's output makes the 'small beats big' point visually.
demo_idea: Lab: a 'synthetic dataset engine' script: Z-Image-Turbo renders N bottle/packaging scenes from a prompt grid, CapRL-2B writes dense captions via mlx-vlm, DINOv3 dedupes, and the result is a HF-style JSONL/parquet you can push as a dataset; the README shows caption quality on a real beu render including label text. Side benefit for beu: caption the existing render library once and get free text search over product shots.
mac_evidence: Official README/HF card never mention MLX/Apple/Metal/CoreML; the only recommended inference is vLLM ("We recommend using vLLM to speed up inference"), and flash-attn/deepspeed are pinned training deps only. No mlx-community port (author=mlx-community search=CapRL -> 0 results) and no ONNX/Transformers.js port (search=CapRL onnx -> 0). Mac path is nonetheless concrete: (1) InternLM ships an official GGUF repo internlm/CapRL-Qwen3VL-2B-GGUF (arch 'qwen3vl', Q2_K/Q4_K_S/Q4_K_M/Q6_k/Q8_0/f16 plus mmproj-Q8_0/f16 vision projector), and llama.cpp tools/mtmd/clip.cpp references qwen3vl (11 hits), so it runs on Metal via llama.cpp/LM Studio today; (2) the safetensors are standard Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration / model_type qwen3_vl, and mlx-vlm v0.6.17 (2026-08-26) has a full mlx_vlm/models/qwen3_vl package with mlx-community/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct-{4,8}bit ports of the identical architecture, so `mlx_vlm.convert` on the HF repo should work (unverified at runtime, no prebuilt CapRL MLX port). 2.4B BF16 (~5GB) fits trivially in 128GB unified memory.
notes: GitHub: 228 stars, Apache-2.0 SPDX, description "[ICLR 2026] An official implementation of CapRL". The "CapRL-Qwen3VL-2B outperforms both CapRL-Qwen2.5VL-3B and Qwen2.5VL-72B in captioning tasks" claim is the authors' own statement in README line 66 and HF card line 26 (their benchmarks, not independently verified). Candidate summary is accurate on: Apache-2.0, ~2.44B, GGUF builds, qwen3_vl architecture, video extension (CapRL++ / CapRL-Video-4B, 2026). Minor: video weights landed 2026-05-22, paper 2026-06-08. Community GGUFs also exist (mradermacher, prithivMLmods). Caveat for the demo idea: the candidate's "loads in mlx-vlm" is by architecture compatibility only; the ready-to-run Mac path is the official GGUF + mmproj in llama.cpp, or converting to MLX yourself. Downloads are modest (2B: 323, 4B: 3451), so this is a niche but legitimately open model. Freshness: model itself is Dec-2025; the 2026 element is CapRL++ / the video model and the ICLR 2026 acceptance.

demo_idea: sml-lab: mflux (v0.18+, FLUX.2 4B/9B with LoRA + multi-reference editing, 2.4x KV-cache speedup since June 2026) batch script that takes a character reference sheet and a JSON of 8 scene prompts, renders the strip with and without the LoRA, and reports per-panel ArcFace/CLIP similarity to the reference. Publish the strip as a scrolling 'comic' page on the blog.
mac_evidence: mflux (filipstrand/mflux, MIT, 2315 stars, pushed 2026-09-03, v0.19.1 released 2026-08-26) is a native MLX implementation of the exact base: src/mflux/models/flux2/README.md says "MFLUX supports FLUX.2-klein-4B, FLUX.2-klein-9B, and FLUX.2-klein-9b-kv ... All the standard modes such as img2img, LoRA, LyCORIS LoKr, and quantizations are supported for this model. FLUX.2 also supports image-conditioned editing with multi-image support." and "FLUX.2-klein-9B requires ~32GB model weights. Use quantization for smaller sizes" (fine on 128GB unified memory). The LoRA file's safetensors header (inspected via HTTP range) uses ai-toolkit 0.9.1 keys `diffusion_model.double_blocks.N.img_attn.qkv.lora_A.weight` / `diffusion_model.single_blocks.N.linear1.lora_A.weight`, and mflux's tests/lora/test_flux2_lora_mapping.py::test_matches_diffusion_model_double_block_keys asserts exactly those key strings map, so the adapter should load without conversion. mlx-community ports of the base exist: mlx-community/FLUX.2-klein-9B (2026-02-21, 2867 dl), mlx-community/flux2-klein-9b-4bit and -8bit (2026-05-23). No Apple/MLX/CUDA mention at all in the LoRA README (it ships only ComfyUI workflow JSONs), and no CUDA-only kernels are implied by a 331MB rank-64 LoRA. Caveats: (1) no mflux issue or HF discussion documents anyone actually running THIS LoRA in mflux — support is inferred from the key-format test, not a first-hand run; (2) mflux v0.19.1 notes that before that release "Baking a LoRA into a sub-8-bit quantized model silently dropped the adapter" — use q8 or bf16, or mflux >= 0.19.1; (3) open issue #704 (2026-09-02) "flux2-klein-9b: --base-model with local path resolves wrong attention head count (24 vs 32)" affects local-path quantized checkpoints. Not browser: only ONNX/WebGPU ports are 4B (MarkShark2/flux2-klein-4b-onnx-webgpu-q4, cgb/flux2-klein-4b-onnx-webgpu, both 0 downloads) and the LoRA is 9B-only.
notes: Stats confirmed: 478 likes, 45,905 downloads (HF 30-day counter), 53 Spaces (e.g. prithivMLmods/FLUX.2-Klein-LoRA-Studio). Trained with ai-toolkit 0.9.1, 12,000 steps / 77 epochs, single tag "consistency" (hence no trigger word). Secondary claim verified: dx8152/Qwen-Edit-2509-Multiple-angles exists (created 2025-10-31, 976 likes, 160,126 dl, apache-2.0, base Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit-2509, 100 Spaces) — but it is late-2025, not 2026. IMPORTANT correction to the demo_idea: the candidate assumes the mflux "2.4x KV-cache speedup" (v0.18.0, 2026-06-07, applies only to the flux2-klein-9b-kv variant) stacks with this LoRA, but the author explicitly says in HF discussion #3 "Is it compatible with FLUX.2-klein-9b-kv?" -> "Incompatible"; a tester reports it works with the KV model only when KV caching is NOT used. So plan the demo on plain flux2-klein-9b (no KV cache) or validate first. Also HF discussion #12 reports a diffusers user getting a different person than the reference — the LoRA is tuned for ComfyUI workflows (Single image.json / Double Image.json ship in the repo), so prompt/workflow parity matters for the ArcFace-similarity comparison. Base model is non-commercial licensed; a personal blog comic strip is fine but publishing outputs commercially (e.g. beu product shots) is not.

domain: OCR / document parsing

what: Zhipu's GLM-OCR: CogViT encoder + GLM-0.5B decoder, ~0.9B params, scores 94.62 on OmniDocBench v1.5 (top of the leaderboard), handles text, formulas, tables, and JSON information extraction; languages include Korean, Japanese, Chinese, English. mlx-community publishes 4/5/6/8-bit and bf16 MLX weights; mlx-vlm has a native glm_ocr port with task prompts ('Text Recognition:', 'Table Recognition:', JSON schema prompts).

mac_evidence: Official GitHub repo ships examples/mlx-deploy/README.md: "Run GLM-OCR natively on Apple Silicon Macs using mlx-vlm, which leverages the Metal GPU for efficient inference. notes: All URLs in the candidate resolve and the weights/ports are real. One correction to the pitch: "#1 OmniDocBench v1.5" was accurate at launch (94.62 vs PaddleOCR-VL-1.5's 94.5, both self-reported) but PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 (Apache-2.0, released 2026-05-28, also 0.9B, mlx-community ports since 2026-08-12) states it "sets new records on OmniDocBench v1.5" and scores 96.33 on v1.6, so as of 2026-09 GLM-OCR is no longer top of that leaderboard — phrase it as "top of OmniDocBench v1.5 at release" or pair it with PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 in the shootout. For the beu label-extraction demo the JSON-schema prompt path is documented in both the HF card ("Information Extraction — Prompts must follow a strict JSON schema") and the mlx-vlm README. what: Lightricks' LTX-2.3/2.5 audio+video DiT (22B, 8-step distilled variant) plus an official Cinemagraph LoRA (trigger 'CINEMAGRAPH_MOTION', 25 frames at 512x704, only the named element moves, camera locked). ltx-2-mlx is a pure-MLX port of LTX-2.3 and 2.5 with bf16/int8/int4 packs (~42/21/12 GB), --low-ram block streaming, image-to-video, --lora loading and LoRA training; mlx-video and mlx-community/ltx-2.5-mlx also exist.

mac_evidence: ltx-2-mlx README: "Pure MLX port of LTX-2 (LTX-2.3 & LTX-2.5) for Apple Silicon ... running natively on Metal"; Requirements: "macOS with Apple Silicon (M1/M2/M3/M4) ... 32GB+ RAM recommended (int8) or 16GB+ with --low-ram. 16GB minimum (int4 without streaming)"; Pre-converted packs table: bf16 dgrauet/ltx-2.3-mlx ~42 GB (64 GB+), int8 -q8 ~21 GB (32 GB+), int4 -q4 ~12 GB (16 GB+). Modality tiling note: "unblocks long / HD / 4K generations on Mac Studio (64-128 GB)". Issue #40 hardware matrix: "M4 Max 64 GB ... Q4 clean, Q8 clean" (Q4 distilled mosaic artefacts only on M2/M3 GPUs) with a logged run: stage 1 8 steps at 4.22 s/it, stage 2 3 steps at 19.33 s/it, decode 10 s for I2V 1024x576 on M3 Ultra. Issue #86 reports peak-memory measurements on "M4 Max 64 GB, q4 distilled with all 48 blocks resident". cli.py: `generate` subparser has `--lora PATH STRENGTH` (repeatable, local file or HF repo id) and the `--distilled` branch sets `pipe._pending_loras = lora_paths` on DistilledPipeline; changelog: "Enables generate --lora on the --low-ram block-streaming path ... Works for community LoRAs at strength 1.0". No CUDA/flash-attn/xformers requirement anywhere. Separate MLX ports also exist: mlx-community/ltx-2.5-mlx (2026-08-12), mlx-community/ltx-2.5-mlx-q8, prince-canuma/LTX-2.3-distilled via Blaizzy/mlx-video. No ONNX/Transformers.js port found (HF search "ltx-2 onnx" returned 0), so browser is out; this is a local-render-then-serve-webm pipeline.
notes: All six source URLs resolve. GitHub dgrauet/ltx-2-mlx: MIT, 109 stars, active (v0.15.0-0.15.2 shipped 2026-08-27..29). Weights confirmed: Lightricks/LTX-2.3 (ungated) has ltx-2.3-22b-distilled.safetensors, -distilled-1.1, -dev, distilled-lora-384, spatial/temporal upscalers; dgrauet/ltx-2.3-mlx{,-q8,-q4} MLX packs exist (q4 3650 downloads). Lightricks/LTX-2.3-22b-LoRA-Cinemagraph confirmed: base_model Lightricks/LTX-2.3, adapter, pipeline_tag image-to-video, single 201 MB safetensors v0.9, example prompts all start with "CINEMAGRAPH_MOTION, tripod locked-off static camera, zero camera movement, ... only the X moves ... seamless natural loop" (trigger word verified). CAVEATS: (1) The LoRA repo and Lightricks/LTX-2.5 are gated="auto" (click-through "Agree and Access" + marketing consent) so an HF login is needed to download; the raw README returned "Access ... is restricted", so the claimed "25 frames at 512x704" recommended setting could not be verified. (2) The candidate's "Cinemagraph LoRA via ltx-2-mlx" combo is not documented as tested by the port author; what is verified is generic community-LoRA loading on the distilled pipeline (cli + changelog + issue #16 fix "LoRA silently ignored for T2V" resolved). Expect to validate LoRA key remapping yourself. (3) docs/PIPELINES.md: "generate --lora (one-stage) is incompatible with --low-ram"; irrelevant on 128 GB where bf16 pack fits without streaming. (4) LTX-2.5 is a separate 22B model with Gemma-4 text encoder and its own MLX packs; the Cinemagraph LoRA targets 2.3, so use 2.3 packs for this demo. (5) Q4 distilled has known numeric artefacts on M2/M3 GPUs (issue #40) but renders clean on M4 Max; on a 128 GB M4 Max prefer the bf16 or q8 pack anyway. (6) Frame count must be 8k+1 (25 frames = 1.0 s at 24 fps); seamless loop (first frame = last frame) is a prompt/keyframe technique, not a built-in flag, though the `keyframe` subcommand accepts --start and --end images. License: LTX-2 Community License is free commercial under revenue threshold per Lightricks terms; verify current text at the LICENSE link before shipping on a commercial landing page (beu).

released: 2025-05-15 (README changelog: "Released code and a checkpoint of Marigold-IID-Lighting v1.1 / Appearance v1.1"; paper arXiv:2505.09358, May 2025). HF repos created 2024-10-21 (appearance) and 2024-12-16 (lighting), lastModified 2025-05-20. GitHub last push 2026-09-06 (ruff + LCM-trainer merges), 3,203 stars, not archived.
what: Two SD2-based diffusion decomposers from ETH: the 'lighting' checkpoint splits a photo into albedo, diffuse shading and a non-diffuse (specular) residual under I = A*S + R; the 'appearance' checkpoint gives albedo, roughness and metallicity. Available as diffusers MarigoldIntrinsicsPipeline; the official repo has an --apple_silicon MPS flag. A community ONNX export (ShaderError/luxtractor-marigold-iid) also exists.
why_cool: Seeing a glossy cosmetic bottle explode into flat albedo, soft shading and a separate specular layer is instantly legible to a viewer, and it is the precise decomposition that makes glossy relighting tractable (re-shade S, keep or scale R).
demo_idea: blog (formless): an 'intrinsic split' page. Upload a bottle photo, show A / S / R tiles (precomputed on the Mac, or via the ONNX export in ORT-Web as a stretch goal), then recombine in the WebGL hero as A * S' + k*R where S' is re-shaded live from MoGe normals and a draggable light. Visitors watch the shading move while the label's true colour stays fixed.
mac_evidence: Official repo has first-class MPS support: README line 203 "--apple_silicon: Use Apple Silicon MPS acceleration." and script/iid/run.py lines 172-177: `if apple_silicon: if torch.backends.mps.is_available() and torch.backends.mps.is_built(): device = torch.device("mps") else: device = torch.device("cpu")`. requirements.txt is only accelerate, diffusers>=0.25.0, matplotlib, scipy, torch==2.4.1, torchvision, transformers -- no xformers, flash-attn, or NVIDIA-only kernels. Also usable via diffusers MarigoldIntrinsicsPipeline (file confirmed, HTTP 200, examples load prs-eth/marigold-iid-lighting-v1-1 with variant="fp16"). Model card: effective resolution ~768px, DDIM 1-50 steps; an 866M SD2-class UNet at 768px fits trivially in 128GB unified memory. Not claimed as "browser": no mlx-community, CoreML, or Transformers.js port exists (HF searches for marigold+mlx / marigold+coreml return 0); the only ONNX export, ShaderError/luxtractor-marigold-iid (created 2026-07-06, 2 downloads, no model card), ships unet.onnx.data at 3.46 GB fp32 + vae_encoder 137 MB + vae_decoder 198 MB, which exceeds practical ORT-Web/WebGPU buffer limits without a re-export to fp16/int8.
notes: Everything the candidate claims checks out: both HF checkpoints public and ungated with safetensors (full + fp16), official MPS flag, diffusers pipeline integrated, ONNX community export real. Caveats: (1) Release is mid-2025, not 2026 -- the 2026 activity is repo maintenance (ruff, LCM trainer merge on 2026-09-05/06), not a new checkpoint; still the reference open intrinsic-decomposition model. (2) Weights are OpenRAIL++-M (SD2), which carries use restrictions -- fine for a personal blog demo but worth noting. (3) The ONNX export's config.json declares steps: 1, timestep 999, v_prediction, targets [albedo, shading, residual] -- i.e. it is a single-step lighting-model export, so the demo idea of precomputing A/S/R on the Mac and shipping tiles to the WebGL hero is the realistic path; in-browser inference would need a custom fp16 ONNX re-export and is a stretch. (4) Related community mirrors AEmotionStudio/marigold-iid-{appearance,lighting}-v1-1 (2026-03) exist but add nothing over the originals. HF Space demo: huggingface.co/spaces/prs-eth/marigold-iid.

name: MoGe-3 on MLX (metric point map + depth + normals + intrinsics)
domain: depth and surface normals / monocular 3D geometry
license: MIT
params: ViT-L: 370M (HF safetensors total 370,284,399, fp32 ~1.48 GB); ViT-g: 1.25B (HF total 1,250,741,135, fp32 ~5.0 GB)
released: 2026-08-18 (MoGe-3 release per README News + HF createdAt for Ruicheng/moge-3-vitl and -vitg); MLX port 2026-09-02, shipped in mlx-vlm v0.7.0 on 2026-09-07
what: Microsoft's MoGe-3 (Aug 2026) returns a metric 3D point map, depth, normal map, valid mask, and camera intrinsics from a single image in one forward pass, with self-guided sparse volumetric refinement for fine detail. The PyTorch release is CUDA-only (FlexGEMM/Triton), but mlx-vlm ships a pure-MLX port (sparse conv re-implemented) with mlx-community/moge-3-vitl-mlx-fp32 and vitg weights.
why_cool: One product photo becomes a relightable 3D surface: normals let you sweep a virtual light across a bottle and the point map gives true per-pixel 3D coordinates. MIT licensed, three weeks old, and the only way to run it locally is exactly this user's stack (Apple Silicon + MLX).
demo_idea: beu: 'relight and wrap'. Run MoGe3Predictor on a cosmetic bottle shot on the Mac, export normal map + point map + mask as PNG/EXR, then in the beu WebGL (ogl) viewer do deferred shading from the normal map with a draggable key light, and project the label design onto the point-map surface so it follows the container's curvature instead of a flat overlay. Compare against DA3 depth-only wrapping in a lab post. Blog bonus: a self-portrait normal map driving a fake studio light on the cover.
mac_evidence: Upstream README is explicit that the PyTorch path is not for Mac: "macOS is not supported: MoGe-3 depends on FlexGEMM, which builds on Triton, and Triton publishes no macOS wheels"; pyproject pins torch to the CUDA 13.0 wheel index, default device "cuda". But the MLX port exists and is released: mlx_vlm/models/moge3/ (README, config.py, conv_stack.py, convert.py, generate.py, geometry.py, moge3.py, processing_moge3.py, refiner.py) committed 2026-09-02 (052cab9 "Add MoGe-3 monocular geometry estimation model") and present in the v0.7.0 tag (PyPI 0.7.0, 2026-09-07). Its README: "The sparse 3D UNet refiner normally depends on FlexGEMM (Triton, CUDA-only). Here the submanifold convolution, mean pooling, and nearest upsample are re-implemented in pure MLX with sort + binary-search + gather, so the model runs on Apple silicon." Weights: mlx-community/moge-3-vitl-mlx-fp32 (model.safetensors, 370M F32, library_name mlx, config model_type moge3) and mlx-community/moge-3-vitg-mlx-fp32 (1.25B F32), both created 2026-09-02. HF card: "Validated against the torch reference (CPU, fp32): identical valid-pixel masks and <0.2% median relative depth error." No ONNX/Transformers.js port of MoGe-3 exists (only moge-2-*-normal-onnx from 2025), so browser is out.
notes: All five source URLs resolve. GitHub microsoft/MoGe: 2,889 stars, pushed 2026-08-19, LICENSE file is MIT (GitHub API reports NOASSERTION only because the file has a DINOv2 Apache-2.0 carve-out for moge/model/modules/dinov2). Original checkpoints Ruicheng/moge-3-vitl and -vitg are model.pt (MIT, cardData.license=mit). Corrections to candidate: ViT-g is ~1.25B, not ~1.1B; ViT-L is 370M. The mlx-vlm port is 6 days old with 40-42 downloads per repo, one contributor commit, and no published Apple-Silicon latency numbers; the pure-MLX sparse-conv refiner (sort/binary-search/gather) could be slow at resolution_level=9 with refine_steps=3 on M4 Max, so budget for benchmarking. The TF32 note applies to M5+ only; M4 Max runs true fp32. Usage API confirmed: load("mlx-community/moge-3-vitl-mlx-fp32"), MoGe3Predictor(model, processor).infer(read_image(...), resolution_level=9) returns points/depth/mask/normal/intrinsics. The beu demo (normal map + point map export to ogl for deferred relighting and curved label projection) is consistent with the outputs; the browser side would consume exported PNG/EXR, not run the model in-page.

(2) HF API lists 8 mlx-community ports created 2026-08-12: North-Micro-Vision-Instruct-{4bit,5bit,6bit,8bit,mxfp4,mxfp8,nvfp4,bf16}, all tagged 'mlx', 'mlx-vlm', 'cohere_compass'. (5) No ONNX / Transformers.js / GGUF port found (HF search 'North-Micro-Vision onnx', 'gguf', onnx-community: 0 results), so NOT browser-feasible; a litert-community port (int4/wi8 .litertlm) exists for on-device LiteRT but not web.
notes: All candidate claims confirmed against HF API, HF blog, and GitHub: public, ungated, apache-2.0, image-text-to-text, 137 likes / 53K downloads, model_type cohere_compass, 262,144-token vocab, 128K LM context (8K validated multimodal), 11 languages incl. Korean. Native-resolution cap confirmed in blog: "1654 × 2339 pixels, corresponding to an A4 page at 200 dpi". Grounding boxes confirmed: "[x1, y1, x2, y2] on a normalized 0–1000 scale". Architecture confirmed: 400M encoder custom-trained from SigLIP 2 SO400M, 2B Command A+ style LLM (3 sliding-window + 1 global attention layers), DeepStack multi-layer injection. name: PIXLRelight (Oxford PIXL, 2026)
domain: Feed-forward controllable relighting via intrinsic conditioning
license: Code: MIT (GitHub spdx). Weights: CC-BY-NC-4.0 (HF cardData.license) — non-commercial only. Third-party ONNX export also CC-BY-NC-4.0.
params: 640M (HF safetensors reports 640,849,510 total, F32, 2.56 GB; paper says ~640M)
released: 2026-05-18 (arXiv 2605.18735); HF weights 2026-05-19; GitHub first commit 2026-05-20
what: A transformer neural renderer (ViT branch on the source image, ConvNeXt branch on target intrinsics, DPT head predicting per-pixel affine modulation) that relights a photo in under 0.1 s. Target lighting is given either as a reference photo (decomposed by Marigold-IID-Lighting) or as Blender Cycles passes of a coarse proxy lit with user-placed PBR lights. Uses Depth Anything 3 / DINOv3 features.
why_cool: Sub-100 ms relighting with actual PBR light placement is the closest open thing to a 'drag a spotlight over the photo' tool; the light-transfer mode ('make my bottle lit like this reference shot') is a one-click wow.
demo_idea: lab repo only (NC weights): a 'steal this lighting' notebook. Pick a reference product photo as target.jpg, your bottle as source.jpg, patch --device to mps, and measure latency on the M4 Max; then try Mode 2 with a Blender proxy (cylinder + plane) and a spot light swept across 8 angles to produce a light-drag GIF.
mac_evidence: src/models/pixl_relight.py L145-149 auto-selects device: `"cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "mps" if torch.backends.mps.is_available() else "cpu"` and falls to float32 on non-CUDA (L151-155). src/layers/attention.py uses only torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention (no flash-attn/xformers). src/rgbx/inference.py wraps enable_xformers_memory_efficient_attention in try/except ImportError ("run without xformers"). requirements.txt: torch>=2.3, torchvision, numpy<2, opencv-python, diffusers>=0.29, transformers, safetensors — nothing CUDA-only. infer.py `--device` default is `cuda` but accepts `mps` directly (L316, L324) — no patching needed. Memory: renderer 2.56 GB fp32 + Marigold-IID-Lighting v1-1 fp16 (SD2-based, 1 denoise step) fits trivially in 128 GB. Counter-evidence: the sub-0.1 s claim is "forward-pass wall-clock on an NVIDIA RTX A6000" (paper Sec. 4); config uses `pos_embed_rope_dtype: bf16` and `norm_layer: layernormbf16` which need MPS bf16 support (PyTorch >=2.3 on macOS 14+, fine on M4 Max but I did not execute it). No mlx-community port (search returned []). Browser: Reza2kn/PIXLRelight-ONNX (2026-05-28) has webgpu/fp16 (1.29 GB) and int4 MatMulNBits (474 MB) exports of the renderer core only — inputs are [B,3,512,512] source + [B,9,512,512] precomputed intrinsics, Marigold not included; 5 downloads, 0 likes, no demo, so not treated as verified browser feasibility.
notes: All 4 sources resolve. GitHub: 72 stars, single "first commit" 2026-05-20, no pushes since (as of 2026-09-08) — low maintenance signal. HF: 774 downloads, 3 likes. Mode 1 (reference-photo light transfer) is fully self-contained: Marigold-IID-Lighting (prs-eth/marigold-iid-lighting-v1-1) is bundled and downloaded automatically. Mode 2 (PBR light placement) is NOT self-contained: the repo only consumes 13 Blender Cycles EXR passes; the Depth Anything 3 -> mesh -> Blender proxy pipeline from paper Fig. 3 is not in the repo, so the "drag a spotlight" demo requires the user to build that pipeline themselves. HF card Limitations: "trained on indoor scenes" (MIT Multi-Illumination) and "does not synthesise content not present in the source — strong cast shadows or specular highlights ... may not transfer faithfully" — the beu cosmetic-bottle use case (glossy product shots) is out-of-distribution and specular transfer is exactly the weak spot. Per-pixel affine modulation (gain+bias) means output is at native resolution. Candidate's original "mac-slow" call is more conservative than the code evidence; expect seconds-not-milliseconds on MPS but no blocker. The int4 ONNX export (474 MB) makes a WebGPU demo conceivable for the blog if intrinsics are precomputed offline for a fixed source image, but that is untested by anyone visible and the NC weights license applies.

name: Qwen-Image-Edit-2509/2511 + Relight LoRA (dx8152) via mflux
domain: Diffusion relighting (instruction-controlled light direction/quality)
license: Apache-2.0 (LoRA, HF cardData.license) + Apache-2.0 (Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit-2509 and -2511, HF cardData.license) + Apache-2.0 (lightx2v/Qwen-Image-Lightning) + MIT (mflux, GitHub spdx_id)
params: 20,430,401,088 (20.4B BF16, HF safetensors.total for Qwen-Image-Edit-2509 and -2511) + 236,117,032-byte LoRA (Qwen-Edit-Relight.safetensors, x-linked-size)
released: LoRA: 2025-10-23 (HF createdAt), last modified 2025-11-12. Base Qwen-Image-Edit-2509: 2025-09-22; -2511: 2025-12-17. mflux v0.19.1: 2026-08-26 (repo pushed 2026-09-03). mlx-community 8-bit edit ports: 2026-05-23.
what: A 236 MB LoRA on top of Apache-2.0 Qwen-Image-Edit that relights a photo from a text instruction (trigger word 重新照明 + a description such as 'soft window light from the upper-left'). mflux runs Qwen-Image-Edit with LoRAs natively on MLX, so the whole stack is Apache-2.0 and Apple-Silicon native.

demo_idea: beu: an mflux batch script that takes each bottle render/photo and produces a 4-up lighting sheet (softbox top-left, hard rim light from behind, warm window light, overcast) with the Lightning LoRA at 4-8 steps; expose it as a before/after slider on the beu product page and time per-image latency on the M4 Max for a blog note.
mac_evidence: mflux (mflux-community/mflux, MIT, 2315 stars, pushed 2026-09-03, v0.19.1 2026-08-26) src/mflux/models/qwen/README.md: 'Qwen Image Edit ... works seamlessly with LoRA adapters' and a documented CLI example `mflux-generate-qwen-edit --lora-paths "lightx2v/Qwen-Image-Lightning" "dx8152/Qwen-Edit-2509-Multiple-angles" --lora-scales 0.5 1.0 --steps 8` — same author/base family and same code path as the Relight LoRA. No CUDA/flash-attn/xformers requirement anywhere in the MLX path. No timing numbers are published in the README (README table only says 'Large model (slower)'). Newer '2511' relight LoRAs on HF (Kun1009, sleziak) have 0-19 downloads and are not credible replacements. Expect slow per-image latency (20B DiT, README calls it 'Large model (slower)'); measuring it on the M4 Max is a legitimate blog datapoint since none is published.

domain: super-resolution & restoration

params: SeedVR2-3B ~3B (upstream fp32 seedvr2_ema_3b.pth 13.57 GB + ema_vae.pth 1.0 GB; mflux uses fp16 safetensors 6.78 GB + 0.5 GB VAE; int8 MLX 4.2 GB). SeedVR2-7B also available (fp16 16.48 GB). Swin2SR realworld x4 ~12-13M (fp32 ONNX 53.8 MB, fp16 28.3 MB, q4f16 15.2 MB).

Swin2SR ONNX re-export 2026-01-03 (base model caidas/swin2SR-realworld-sr-x4-64-bsrgan-psnr is Dec 2022, paper Sep 2022).
what: ByteDance's SeedVR2 is a one-step diffusion restoration/upscaling model (3B and 7B, Apache-2.0) that mflux runs natively on Apple Silicon (`--resolution 2x/3x` or up to 2160, quantize=8, --low-ram flag for big outputs). For the client side, onnx-community published swin2SR-realworld-sr-x4 (Jan 2026, Apache-2.0) which runs in Transformers.js's image-to-image pipeline at only 15 MB q4f16 / 28 MB fp16.
why_cool: A before/after slider where a blurry 400px packaging photo becomes crisp 4K in one diffusion step is the most legible 'AI did that' moment for non-technical viewers; pairing a 15 MB browser upscaler with a 3B Mac model shows the whole spectrum.
demo_idea: beu: batch-restore low-res supplier/packaging photos on the Mac with SeedVR2 (mflux) before laying designs on them. Blog: an interactive slider that upscales the visitor's own image client-side with Swin2SR x4 (15 MB), plus a lab post comparing Swin2SR-in-browser vs SeedVR2-on-MLX on the same crops with timings.
mac_evidence: mflux (MIT, 2,315 stars, pushed 2026-09-03) ships a native MLX implementation: src/mflux/models/seedvr2/README.md — "MFLUX's MLX implementation of the SeedVR2 upscaler", CLI `mflux-upscale-seedvr2 --image-path input.png --resolution 2160|2x|3x --softness 0.5`, `--model seedvr2-7b`, `--low-ram`, `--mlx-cache-limit-gb 16`; seedvr2_upscale.py line 99 passes `quantize=args.quantize` and seedvr2_initializer.py applies `WeightApplier.apply_and_quantize` (so -q 8 works). Weights it downloads: numz/SeedVR2_comfyUI (apache-2.0) seedvr2_ema_3b_fp16.safetensors 6.78 GB + ema_vae_fp16.safetensors 0.50 GB — trivially fits 128 GB unified memory. Independent MLX ports also exist: mlx-community/SeedVR2-3B-mlx (fp16 transformer 7.9 GB, created 2026-06-06, tags mlx/apple-silicon) and mlx-community/SeedVR2-3B-mlx-int8 (4.2 GB), for xocialize/seedvr2-mlx-swift (macOS 14+/iOS 17+); benc0/SeedVR2-7B-mlx (2026-07-09). SeedVR2 integration first landed 2025-12-31 (#297, v0.14.0) and was last fixed 2026-08-31 (#690 "SeedVR2 upscaling crashes on mlx 0.32.2"). Caveat: no README publishes Apple Silicon timings, so speed is unmeasured (one-step diffusion, 3B DiT). Browser half: onnx-community/swin2SR-realworld-sr-x4-64-bsrgan-psnr-ONNX has library_name transformers.js, pipeline image-to-image, onnx/model_q4f16.onnx 15.2 MB, model_fp16.onnx 28.3 MB, model.onnx 53.8 MB; transformers.js packages/transformers/src/models/swin2sr/modeling_swin2sr.js defines Swin2SRForImageSuperResolution (v4.2.0 released 2026-04-23).
notes: All four source URLs resolve. Corrections to the candidate text: (1) mflux does NOT load the 13.5 GB fp32 .pth from ByteDance-Seed; model_config.py sets model_name="numz/SeedVR2_comfyUI" and downloads the fp16 safetensors (6.78 GB), so download/quantize-on-load cost is about half what the candidate states. (2) The HF ByteDance-Seed repo is video-to-video and bundles CUDA-only apex linux_x86_64 wheels — the upstream codebase is GPU-only; Mac feasibility comes entirely from mflux / the MLX-Swift port, which expose single-image upscaling (no video path on Mac). (3) `--low-ram` is explicitly "not supported when upscaling a directory" (README warning) — irrelevant on 128 GB but affects the beu batch idea if reused on a smaller Mac. (4) mflux v.0.19.1 (2026-08-26, latest release) crashes SeedVR2 on mlx 0.32.2 (issue #690, fixed on main 2026-08-31, unreleased at check time) — pin mlx 0.32.0/0.32.1 or install mflux from main. (5) The browser half is not new: Swin2SR is a 2022 model, Xenova/swin2SR-realworld-sr-x4-64-bsrgan-psnr has existed since 2023-11 (4,302 downloads); the onnx-community repo (79 downloads, 2 likes) is just a Jan 2026 auto-conversion via the convert-to-onnx Space. Still the correct pick for a 15 MB in-page upscaler, but the "2026" framing applies only to the re-export. (6) No Apple Silicon timing/benchmark exists in any README or card — the "one step" claim is from the paper; actual seconds-per-image on M4 Max must be measured. (7) Other ports found: Merserk/SeedVR2-3B-ONNX (MIT, 2026-06-18, 6.8 GB, DirectML/WindowsML-targeted — not browser-viable); avencera/swin2sr-native-mlx (2026-08-26, native MLX Swin2SR classical x2/x4, no license set). No mlx-community Swin2SR port. GitHub stats: ByteDance-Seed/SeedVR 1,350 stars, pushed 2026-01-27; transformers.js 16,289 stars, pushed 2026-09-07.

domain: single image -> textured PBR mesh (GLB)
license: MIT (microsoft/TRELLIS.2 code: GitHub spdx MIT; microsoft/TRELLIS.2-4B weights: HF cardData license mit; trellis-mac: spdx MIT). what: Microsoft's MIT-licensed 4B image-to-3D model (Dec 2025) producing 1536-res assets with PBR (base color, metallic, roughness) textures; trellis-mac (MIT, Apr 2026, 478 stars) ports the full pipeline to PyTorch MPS with a Metal texture baker: ~5 min per object on an M4 Pro 24GB, 18 GB peak, GLB output.
why_cool: A photographed bottle becomes a spinnable, relightable 3D object with real metallic caps and glossy glass in minutes, on a Mac, no CUDA. Dropped into a WebGL page it is the most memorable kind of product demo.
demo_idea: beu + formless: 'photo to turntable'. Run trellis-mac on a client's bottle photo, load the GLB in ogl on the beu page with the page's generative hero as the environment light, and let the user swap the base-color texture with a label PNG (from Boogu/Ideogram) to preview packaging on the real 3D shape. Do the cutout client-side first with onnx-community/BiRefNet_dynamic-1024x1024-ONNX (Sept 2026) in Transformers.js v4.
mac_evidence: Upstream is hard-CUDA: microsoft/TRELLIS.2 README says "The code is currently tested only on Linux", "An NVIDIA GPU with at least 24GB of memory is necessary", default attention is flash-attn (xformers alternative), plus nvdiffrast/nvdiffrec/cumesh/flex_gemm CUDA extensions; timing table (512³ ~3s, 1024³ ~17s, 1536³ ~60s) is "Tested on NVIDIA H100 GPU". The Mac path exists only via community ports: shivampkumar/trellis-mac (MIT, 479 stars, created 2026-04-19, last push 2026-04-28) README: "port ... from CUDA-only to Apple Silicon via PyTorch MPS. No NVIDIA GPU required", "~5 minutes 13 seconds on M4 Pro (24GB, cold start ... pipeline type 512)", "Memory usage peaks at around 18GB unified memory", "24GB+ unified memory recommended", flash_attn replaced by padded PyTorch SDPA ("the single largest remaining bottleneck"), Metal texture baker via mtldiffrast/mtlbvh/mtlgemm. Why not plain mac-native: it is ~100x slower than the reference GPU (3s vs ~3.5 min generation at 512³); pipeline options are only 512/1024/1024_cascade (no 1536 on Mac); "Hole filling disabled ... Output meshes may have small holes"; mesh is decimated 800K→200K faces before bake; README warns thermal throttling made "the same run taking 6–10× longer"; issue #9: flex_gemm metallib "is OSX26 only"; issue #8 (open): M2 Ultra decoder "silently produces empty mesh" due to Metal GPU watchdog. notes: All URLs resolve. microsoft/TRELLIS.2: 11,079 stars, MIT, not archived, pushed 2026-07-10. HF microsoft/TRELLIS.2-4B: 1.76M downloads, 1,181 likes, safetensors + pipeline.json + texturing_pipeline.json. Candidate claims check out with small corrections: trellis-mac has 479 stars (not 478) and has had no commits since 2026-04-28 with 7 open issues, so it is a one-month burst port, not a maintained project; 1536-res is upstream/H100 only, trellis-mac tops out at 1024_cascade. For an MLX-first lab the more relevant repo is pedronaugusto/trellis2-apple (actual MLX backend, MIT, pushed 2026-08-06) whose Metal kernels trellis-mac reuses. Licensing matters for beu (commercial): the default preprocessing uses RMBG-2.0 (CC BY-NC); the demo idea's client-side BiRefNet cutout sidesteps that only if the pre-cut RGBA image bypasses RMBG in the pipeline — generate.py has no rmbg/alpha flag (grep found none), so this needs verification in the patched pipeline's preprocess_image. BiRefNet ONNX side is verified: onnx-community/BiRefNet_dynamic-1024x1024-ONNX exists, MIT, created 2026-09-01, tagged transformers.js, ships onnx/model.onnx and onnx/model_fp16.onnx (only 39 downloads, very new). User's Mac Studio M4 Max 128GB on Darwin 25.6 (macOS 26) satisfies the flex_gemm metallib requirement and the 24GB+ memory floor; expect a few minutes per object, run it offline as a batch step and serve the GLB, not as a live demo. GGUF variants exist for ComfyUI (Aero-Ex/Trellis2-GGUF, Comfy-Org/TRELLIS.2) but are CUDA-oriented.

name: TripoSplat (VAST-AI / Tripo)
domain: single image -> 3D Gaussian splat (object)
license: MIT for code and TripoSplat-trained weights (GitHub SPDX MIT; HF cardData license: mit; LICENSE file "Copyright (c) 2026 VAST"). Bundled third-party files carry their own terms: (a) vae/flux2-vae.safetensors is byte-identical (sha256 d64f3a68...) to black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-dev vae (flux-non-commercial-license), BUT I verified all 251 tensors are numerically identical to the Apache-2.0, ungated black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-klein-4B VAE (max rel diff 0.27% = fp32→bf16 rounding, same 84,046,372 params, same keys) — load the VAE from klein-4B for a clean commercial chain; (b) clip_vision/dino_v3_vit_h.safetensors is Meta's DINOv3 ViT-H/16+ under the DINOv3 License (commercial allowed, license text must accompany redistribution — per the mlx-community card, not independently checked); (c) birefnet.safetensors MIT. mlx-community/tripo_splat_mlx itself is tagged "license: other (mixed-see-license-section)".
params: 1.58B on the inference path, measured from safetensors headers: DINOv3 ViT-H/16+ 0.841B (bf16) + flow DiT 0.371B (fp16, 741 MB) + FLUX.2 VAE encoder 0.084B + octree Gaussian decoder 0.288B; plus BiRefNet 0.221B and a training-only TripoSplat VAE encoder 0.338B → 2.14B / 4.46 GB for the full HF repo. (Candidate's "~1.3B" undercounts; decoder alone is 0.29B.)
released: Paper arXiv 2605.16355 v1 2026-05-08 (arXiv comments: "SIGGRAPH Conference Papers '26"); HF weights repo created 2026-05-31; GitHub repo 2026-06-01; HF Space 2026-06-01; last GitHub push 2026-08-13; mlx-community port 2026-07-23.
what: Feed-forward generative model that turns one RGBA product/object image into a variable-count (up to 262,144) 3D Gaussian splat in one pass; exports .ply/.splat/.spz that load directly in SparkJS or SuperSplat. SIGGRAPH 2026 (arXiv 2605.16355), code+weights MIT, ~2,000 lines of plain PyTorch with no diffusers/transformers/flash-attn.
why_cool: A visitor uploads one photo and a few seconds later a photoreal object spins in the browser with real view-dependent shading, not a baked mesh; the splat count slider lets you trade quality for load time live.
demo_idea: beu: photograph a cosmetic bottle on white, cut it out with BiRefNet, run mlx-community/tripo_splat_mlx (DINOv3 + VAE + flow on MLX, decoder on MPS), compress to .spz and embed with Spark so the product spins on drag inside the beu page; second pass: apply the label design in beu first, then splat the mock-up so the client sees their artwork in 3D.
mac_evidence: (1) Upstream README: "Near-zero dependencies: no transformers, no diffusers ... Runs on any platform"; install is "pip install numpy safetensors pillow tqdm" plus torch/torchvision. Source (2,523 LOC) uses only F.scaled_dot_product_attention — no flash-attn/xformers/triton/custom CUDA kernels; device is a plain ctor arg (`TripoSplatPipeline(..., device="cuda")`, `self._device = torch.device(device)`), so "mps" is a one-word change. (2) mlx-community/tripo_splat_mlx (created 2026-07-23, tags mlx/apple-silicon): "MLX-native implementation of TripoSplat for Apple Silicon ... MLX ports: DinoV3 ViT-H/16+ encoder, Flux2 VAE encoder, LatentSeqMMFlowModel (24-block flow transformer). The original TripoSplat decoder (OctreeGaussianDecoder) remains on PyTorch MPS." (3) Jup33Q/TripoSplat-Klein-MLX README: "Requirements: macOS 14+ on Apple Silicon (M1/M2/M3/M4)"; code defaults `triposplat_backend: str = "mps"`; R3F web UI + Bilibili video demo of the hybrid MLX/MPS pipeline; decode density selectable up to 1,048,576 Gaussians ("substantially increase unified-memory usage").
