name: metal-gauss (with msplat as the Swift/C++ sibling)
domain: Metal-native 3DGS training on Apple Silicon
license: MIT (metal-gauss, GitHub spdx MIT); Apache-2.0 (rayanht/msplat, GitHub spdx Apache-2.0); Apache-2.0 (zacsmms/mpsplat)
params: n/a — trainer/optimiser, no pretrained weights
released: metal-gauss: repo created 2026-08-26, first commit "Hello world" 2026-08-31, last push 2026-09-06, no tags/releases, not on PyPI (install via pip git+). msplat: repo created 2026-03-05, releases v1.1.2 (2026-03-05) → v1.1.4 (2026-08-25), on PyPI 1.1.4.
what: MIT trainer that compiles Metal compute kernels at runtime through PyTorch MPS (`torch.mps.compile_shader`, no CUDA, no Xcode): fused forward/backward rasteriser, SSIM, Adam, densification. Takes COLMAP or Blender inputs, exports standard INRIA .ply, and ships a renderer that can also fly a SHARP single-image splat 'like-photo'. Its Sept-2026 benchmark shows 24.7 dB PSNR in 1 minute on NeRF-synthetic vs Brush 14.4 / msplat 20.8. msplat (Apache-2.0) is the pure-Metal C++/Swift equivalent: ~70 s for a full Mip-NeRF 360 scene, ~350 FPS on M4 Max.
why_cool: For the first time a Mac trains a splat in a minute, not an hour — the numbers are published head-to-head against Brush, msplat and spirula, all measured on Apple Silicon.
demo_idea: sml-lab post 'Splat a cosmetic bottle in 60 seconds on M4 Max': same COLMAP capture through metal-gauss, msplat and Brush, plot PSNR vs wall-clock, publish the three .ply files side by side in one Spark page. Bonus: msplat's Swift package could become a native beu capture app.
mac_evidence: metal-gauss README: "3D Gaussian Splatting that trains on Apple Silicon. Metal kernels, no CUDA, no Xcode" and "macOS on Apple Silicon, Python >=3.10, PyTorch >=2.5. Metal kernels compile at runtime — no Xcode". pyproject deps: torch>=2.5, numpy, plyfile, ninja, pillow, scipy (no CUDA deps). CI Metal job: `runs-on: macos-15`. metal_backend.py: `torch.utils.cpp_extension.load(... extra_ldflags=["-framework","Metal","-framework","Foundation"])`; rasterize.mm: "The .metal source is compiled at runtime with newLibraryWithSource" — CUDA appears only in torch_ref.py/benchmark harness references. msplat README: "built entirely on Metal. No external dependencies beyond system frameworks... Requires macOS 14+, Apple Silicon"; GitHub release v1.1.4 ships msplat-1.1.4-cp312/cp313-macosx_14_0_arm64.whl + MsplatCore.xcframework.zip; benchmarks explicitly "M4 Max". HF checks: author=mlx-community search metal-gauss/msplat → [], any search → [], onnx → [] (not applicable: no model weights). Browser is out of scope for the trainer itself; only its standard INRIA .ply output is viewable in a web splat viewer.
notes: CONFIRMED claims: MIT; COLMAP (--colmap, needs optional pycolmap) and Blender inputs; standard INRIA .ply export; fused Metal preprocess/rasterize/SSIM/Adam + MCMC densification (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md); metal-gauss-render `--like-photo` reproduces Apple SHARP's EXIF f_35mm→f_px conversion and README notes SHARP's own video renderer requires CUDA ("predict on MPS, render here"). Budget table matches exactly: 1 min = metal-gauss 24.7 / msplat 20.8 / Brush 14.4 / spirula 15.1 dB (8-scene NeRF-synthetic mean); 3 min 29.8, 15 min 31.9. msplat: "~70 seconds ... ~350 FPS on an M4 Max" verbatim; per-scene 7K no-downscale bicycle 59s / counter 80s / garden 77s / room 74s, garden 30K 700s (3.51M gaussians). INACCURACIES in candidate: (1) it does NOT use `torch.mps.compile_shader` — grep finds zero occurrences; it is a torch cpp_extension (.mm Objective-C++) built by ninja/clang on first import (Command Line Tools required, so "no Xcode" is true but there IS a compile step), with the .metal source compiled at runtime via `newLibraryWithSource`. (2) Benchmarks are from an M5, not M4 Max: README render FPS "on an M5", result file bench/results/bench_m5_270x480.json — the 1-minute figure is not an M4 Max measurement. (3) "1 minute" is on 800px NeRF-synthetic at 2000 iterations, not a real-scene capture; README caveats: "do not lean on that +0.5 dB" (three scenes cleared 60 s by 0.5–2.2 s, and did not on re-measure), competitor rows predate the loader re-measurement, msplat is "1.3–1.8x faster per step", msplat noise floor 3.35 dB (no seed flag), wall-clock rows need an idle machine (57–68 s idle vs 74–96 s with a browser open), 7k not comparable to published 30k. Maturity risk: metal-gauss is ~2 weeks old, 21 commits, 40 stars, 3 forks, single author, no tags/releases, hatchling "Development Status :: 4 - Beta"; msplat 70 stars / 28 forks, Python wheels need Python >=3.12 and Swift package needs Xcode + CMake (`./scripts/build-xcframework.sh`). Third source zacsmms/mpsplat is a low-activity gsplat fork (3 stars, last push 2026-05-12). weights_available=false is by nature (optimiser, not a model); code is fully available, which is what verification rests on. Demo idea holds: same COLMAP capture → metal-gauss / msplat .ply, view in a browser splat viewer; the "60 seconds on M4 Max" headline must be re-measured locally rather than quoted.

Final compositing is a per-pixel Python getpixel/putpixel loop (trivially replaceable with numpy). Preprocessing needs mask (SAM), depth/normal (Marigold), and diffuse shading (Marigold-IID) — Marigold-IID is a separate heavier model; swapping to DA3/BiRefNet covers depth+mask but a shading estimator is still required. Commercial caveat: base FLUX.1-dev + Redux are non-commercial, so a beu product use would need a FLUX Pro/Klein license or a different base. Overnight precompute of an 8-swatch grid is realistic on the Mac Studio; live in-page inference is not.

demo_idea: beu: after the label/design overlay is placed on a bottle and dropped onto a new backdrop, run libcom's ShadowGenerationModel on MPS to add the contact shadow, sample 4 seeds (the authors note instability) and keep the one whose direction agrees with the light chosen in the relight step.
mac_evidence: Nothing runs on a Mac as shipped; it becomes runnable only after small device patches, and then it is slow. Evidence: (1) libcom README: "The main branch is built on the Linux system with Python 3.10 and PyTorch>=2.6." (2) libcom/shadow_generation/shadow_generation.py line 447: `self.device = torch.device(f"cuda:{device}" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")` - no MPS branch, so on a Mac it silently falls to CPU; line 448 `self.weight_dtype = torch.float32`. (3) Line 563: `load_state_dict(self.ppp_weight_path, location='cuda')` which calls `torch.load(ckpt_path, map_location=torch.device('cuda'))` in source/cldm/model.py - a hard RuntimeError on any machine without CUDA, so the constructor crashes before inference. (4) Inference is 50 denoising steps of SDXL UNet + ControlNet + IP-Adapter at fixed 512x512 in fp32, and `__call__` defaults to number=5 samples (50 steps each). (5) Standalone SD1.5 repo infer_GPSDiffusion.py hard-codes `torch.cuda.set_device`, `.cuda()`, `location='cuda'`; both repos' requirements.txt pin `xformers==0.0.27.post2` and `torch==2.4.0` (no macOS xformers wheel), plus mmdet==3.3.0. (6) SDXL repo test_GPSDiffusion_sdxl.py is a diffusers/accelerate template that does check `torch.backends.mps.is_available()`, but its post_processing.py hard-codes `torch.cuda.set_device` / `.cuda()`. (7) `from libcom import ShadowGenerationModel` goes through libcom/__init__.py which eagerly imports every task module, so libcom's whole requirements set (mmdet==3.2.0, mmpose==1.2.0, segment_anything, taming-transformers) must install on arm64 macOS. (8) No custom CUDA kernels, flash-attn or triton in the shadow_generation tree - plain diffusers SDXL+ControlNet, which does run on MPS - hence not gpu-only. (9) No MLX port: `api/models?author=mlx-community&search=GPSDiffusion` and `search=shadow` both return []. No ONNX/Transformers.js port found; multi-GB SDXL+ControlNet rules out browser.
notes: Verification: all three GitHub repos resolve (SDXL repo MIT, 66 stars; SD1.5 repo MIT, 152 stars; libcom Apache-2.0, 736 stars). No GitHub releases on either GPSDiffusion repo. Weights: SDXL repo README lists Baidu Cloud ONLY (access code bcmi) - the Dropbox link exists only for the SD1.5 checkpoints and the DESOBAv2 dataset. The real HF source is the official BCMIZB/Libcom_pretrained_models (libcom auto-downloads from it via hf_hub_download with ModelScope fallback): shadow_controlnet.zip 4.6 GB, ip_adapter.ckpt 1.4 GB, Shadow_ppp.ckpt 0.73 GB, Shadow_cls.pth, Shadow_reg.pth, Shadow_cls_label.pkl, plus SD1.5-era Shadow_cldm.ckpt 5.9 GB. The candidate's cited mirror shin-SF/libcom-shadowgen-weights (2025-09-10, 0 downloads, no card) holds only the SD1.5-era set (Shadow_cldm.ckpt + ppp/cls/reg), not the SDXL weights. Two other third-party zip mirrors of the Baidu SDXL package exist: GrigoriiU/GPSDiffusion-SDXL (pretrained_models_sdxl.zip 6.7 GB, 2026-04-05, README says "Downloaded from the original Baidu Cloud source") and nickfransen/GPSDiffusion-SDXL (pretrained_models.zip 6.2 GB, 2025-10-28). No safetensors, GGUF, MLX or ONNX anywhere. Candidate corrections: 'released 2025-06' is right for the SDXL repo; the 2026 activity is libcom integration/bugfix commits (last code change 2026-02-21) and PyPI 0.1.7 (2026-04-26), while the 2026-08-20 pushes are README-only. Quality caveats from the authors: SD1.5 README says "the performance of GPSDiffusion is unstable, so you need to generate multiple results and pick the most satisfactory one"; SDXL README claims "significantly improved output stability" but libcom still defaults to 5 samples. Output is fixed 512x512x3 (libcom resizes inputs to 512), so for beu you must extract the shadow (difference vs. composite, masked outside the object) and upsample/blend it onto the hi-res product shot. Practical Mac path: pip-install libcom deps on arm64 (mmcv is the pain point), patch line 447 to prefer mps and line 563 to location='cpu', consider fp16 and fewer steps; expect minutes per 5-sample call on an M4 Max. Online demo http://libcom.ustcnewly.com/ returns HTTP 200 if a hosted fallback is acceptable.

license: MIT

what: 3B Qwen2.5-VL-based autoregressive SVG generator (image-to-SVG and text-to-SVG) that tokenizes SVG into geometry-aware atomic and segment tokens (2.76x sequence compression) instead of raw XML bytes. Ships an inference pipeline (hivg_infer) with a pure-Python hierarchical detokenizer.

notes:
VERIFIED FACTS: GitHub ximinng/HiVG resolves, license spdx MIT, 763 stars, last push 2026-04-17 (dormant ~5 months). HF xingxm/HiVG-3B-Base is public, ungated, cardData.license=mit, library transformers, model_type qwen2_5_vl, 2 safetensors shards + full tokenizer/processor files, 396 downloads / 11 likes. Project page hy-hivg.github.io returns 200. Code tree has hivg_infer (pipeline/cli/postprocess), hivg_tokenizer (bpe/detokenizer/segment_io/tokens), hivg_metric. Detokenizer (hivg_tokenizer/detokenizer.py) is pure Python (imports only typing + local .tokens), confirming that part of the candidate.

CRITICAL FUNCTIONAL CAVEAT (independently confirmed, not just from the issue): the released checkpoint's added_tokens.json contains 500 `<SEG_0>..<SEG_499>` Level-2 segment tokens (plus 20 cmd, 469 d_, 235 P_, 82 structure/attr tokens), but (a) no `bpe_model.json` / SEG->atomic mapping file exists anywhere in the GitHub tree or the HF siblings list, (b) hivg_infer/postprocess.py `tokens_to_svg` calls `string_to_tokens` then `SVGDetokenizer.detokenize` directly with zero SEG/segment/bpe references, and (c) detokenizer.py has no `SEG_` handling at all. So if the model emits `<SEG_N>` tokens at inference, the public pipeline cannot reconstruct them. Open issue #5 (2026-09-05, no maintainer reply) reports exactly this; open issue #4 (2026-05-13, Chinese, no reply) reports 'very poor' SVG quality using the README script and paper prompts. Maintainer last replied 2026-04-17 (issue #3, fixed AutoModelForCausalLM -> Qwen2_5_VL dispatch). The 'demo sells itself' claim is therefore unproven for the public weights; budget for the possibility that outputs are degraded or that SEG tokens must be constrained/suppressed at decode time. Only the Base checkpoint exists; Instruct / DwT / DwT-RL are still 'Coming Soon' in README and the HF card explicitly says base model, not instruction-tuned.

MINOR CORRECTIONS TO CANDIDATE: vocab is NOT vanilla 151936 — config.json text_config.vocab_size is 152960 (top-level field still says 151936), because 1306 SVG tokens were added and embeddings resized. mlx_vlm.convert for qwen2_5_vl should still work since it reads text_config, but this is untested. transformers_version in config is 4.57.3; the loader emits a 'fix_mistral_regex' tokenizer warning on recent transformers (issue #3 log). cairosvg needs the native cairo lib (brew install cairo) on macOS. arXiv v2 landed 2026-09-07 but the code repo did not move.

Tested on Apple M-series with PyTorch 2.10 and diffusers 0.37 — ~5x speedup over CPU", verified SDPA/Conv2d/GroupNorm/randn on MPS with no NaN/Inf. pipeline_objectclear.py carries diffusers' MPS guards (lines 1804, 1895). name: OmniSVG 1.1 (4B / 8B)
domain: text/image/character-to-SVG generation
license: Apache-2.0 (GitHub spdx_id Apache-2.0; HF cardData.license apache-2.0 on both OmniSVG/OmniSVG1.1_4B and OmniSVG1.1_8B). Sibling training repo OpenVGLab/OmniSVG-train has NO license file (license: null).
params: 4B: ~3.85B (single 7.69 GB bf16 pytorch_model.bin; Qwen2.5-VL-3B, hidden 2048 / 36 layers, vocab resized to 197,000; HF reports no safetensors param count). 8B: 7.94B (GGUF metadata total=7,937,717,760; official 17.23 GB bf16 pytorch_model.bin).
released: 2025-12-02 (HF repos created 2025-12-01, pytorch_model.bin uploaded 2025-12-02, README news line "[2025/12/02] released OmniSVG1.1_8B ... updated OmniSVG1.1_4B"). GitHub last push 2026-03-01 (README: OmniLottie announcement).
what: End-to-end multimodal SVG generator on Qwen2.5-VL (3B->'4B' and 7B->'8B' variants) with a custom SVG token vocabulary; supports text-to-SVG, image-to-SVG and character-reference-to-SVG, from icons up to complex anime-style illustrations. 1.1 weights (Dec 2025) plus MMSVGBench, training code (Dec 31 2025) and a sibling Lottie-animation model OmniLottie (Mar 2026).
why_cool: The most-starred open SVG generator (2.6k stars, HF Space demo) and the only one that reliably produces long, layered, multi-colour illustrations rather than flat icons; the Jul-2025 3B model was already the community reference, 1.1 improved fidelity and added the 8B. Community GGUF conversions of 1.1_8B exist, showing the token stream is llama.cpp-compatible.
demo_idea: beu: 'label pictogram set generator' - prompt 20 packaging pictograms (recyclable, vegan, SPF 50, 'not tested on animals', dropper, pump) in one house style and emit a single SVG sprite sheet that beu overlays on bottle renders; run the 4B in bf16 on MPS (README quotes 17 GB GPU memory - fine in 128 GB unified memory; brew install cairo for cairosvg; CUDA-only wheels in the README must be swapped for the default torch build). Stretch: convert with mlx_vlm (qwen2_5_vl is supported) and keep OmniSVG's Python SVG detokenizer, then publish the MLX weights.
mac_evidence: Nothing hard-CUDA in the architecture: decoder.py is a thin wrapper — `Qwen2_5_VLForConditionalGeneration.from_pretrained(..., torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16, attn_implementation="sdpa", device_map="auto")` + `resize_token_embeddings(197000)`; requirements.txt has no flash-attn/xformers (torch==2.3.0, transformers==4.51.3, CairoSVG). HF card even has a "**macOS:** brew install cairo" step. BUT: (1) both inference.py:28 and app.py:28 hardcode `torch.device("cuda:0" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")` — no MPS branch — and line 29 calls `torch.cuda.is_bf16_supported()` at import, which in the README-pinned torch 2.3.0 does `device = torch.cuda.current_device()` and raises on a non-CUDA build (torch main returns False instead). (2) The only Apple Silicon report is a failure: GitHub issue #36 "Support MPS (Apple Silicon GPU) backend" (2025-12-07, open, 0 comments, no maintainer reply): "The MPS backend doesn't support the Cholesky decomposition operation" — the cholesky call is not in the repo's own code (grep empty), origin unresolved. (3) README cost table: 4B needs 17 GB GPU memory and 4.08/8.68/18.07/37.51/82.70 s per 256/512/1024/2048/4096 tokens on their CUDA GPU; 8B 26 GB — slow even on NVIDIA, worse on MPS. (4) No MLX port: `api/models?author=mlx-community&search=OmniSVG` → []; `search=OmniSVG mlx` → []; `search=OmniSVG onnx` → [] (no Transformers.js path). mlx-vlm v0.6.17 does have a qwen2_5_vl model dir, but its loader only globs `*.safetensors` ("No safetensors found") and the official repos ship only pytorch_model.bin (two HF PRs "Adding safetensors variant" open since 2026-03-25/04-20, unmerged) — so an MLX route needs a manual torch.load → save_pretrained(safe_serialization=True) step first. (5) Three community GGUFs of 8B exist (Serveurperso 2026-06-03, CC-TM 2026-07-13, amandabenson fork 2026-08-11): all a single BF16 file (15.88 GB), arch=qwen2vl, no mmproj, no README, bos/eos = [PAD196998]/[PAD196999] — llama.cpp/Metal could run text-to-SVG only, and the output is [PADnnnnn] placeholder tokens that still need OmniSVG's tokenizer.py/deepsvg to decode to SVG. Net: runnable on a 128 GB Mac in principle (plain Qwen2.5-VL, sdpa, CPU fallback, Metal GGUF), but unconfirmed on Apple Silicon, needs script patching, and is slow by the authors' own numbers.
notes: Verified facts: GitHub 2,606 stars, Apache-2.0, not archived, pushed 2026-03-01. HF Space OmniSVG/OmniSVG-3B RUNNING on ZeroGPU A10G (lastModified 2025-12-03). Training code repo OpenVGLab/OmniSVG-train exists (created 2025-12-29, 42 stars, no license). OmniLottie exists (OpenVGLab/OmniLottie, CVPR 2026, 775 stars, Apache-2.0, pushed 2026-04-06). Corrections to the candidate: weights are pytorch_model.bin only (no safetensors anywhere, including the aoiandroid/OmniSVG1.1_4B mirror); GGUF ports are BF16-only, text-only (no mmproj), undocumented; the 'materially updated in 2026' bar is not met — 1.1 weights are Dec 2025 and the 2026 commits are config.json/README only. Inference-only wrapper: SketchDecoder.forward raises NotImplementedError ("not included in open-source version"). Community quality flags on the 8B HF repo: open discussions "This doesn't work don't waste your time" (2025-12-20) and "It feels like the model has overfitted the training dataset" (2025-12-29), unanswered. Default max_length 1536 tokens; task presets in config.yaml (icon temp 0.5/top_p 0.88, illustration 0.6/0.90, image-to-svg 0.3). For the beu pictogram demo: patch device selection to mps, use current torch (not 2.3.0), expect tens of seconds per icon; batch of 20 icons is minutes, not interactive. name: Pixal3D (TencentARC, SIGGRAPH 2026)

license: MIT (GitHub spdx MIT; HF cardData.license "mit", ungated). Hard dependency on DINOv3 ViT-L/16 (facebook/dinov3-vitl16-pretrain-lvd1689m) which is HF gated=manual, license "other" — access request required for both the CUDA reference and the MLX port. params: Four 1.3B DiTs (ss_flow_img_dit_1_3B_64, slat_flow_img2shape_dit_1_3B_512, slat_flow_img2shape_dit_1_3B_1024, slat_flow_imgshape2tex_dit_1_3B_1024) ≈ 5.2B in flow models, plus DINOv3-L (~300M), MoGe-2 (326M) and shape/texture VAE decoders — candidate's "~3.9B / three DiTs" undercounts. released: 2026-05 (HF repo createdAt 2026-04-30; GitHub created 2026-05-10, initial commit 2026-05-12; arXiv 2605.10922). TRELLIS.2-backbone "main" branch May 2026; multi-view inference + *_mv weights pushed 2026-09-01. Stars 2,265; HF likes 346; last push 2026-09-01.
what: Lifts pixel features into 3D by back-projection so every pixel has a direct 3D correspondence (instead of loose cross-attention), giving sharper geometry and texture that matches the input photo; main branch is built on the TRELLIS.2 backbone with a 1536 px standard / 1024 px low-VRAM mode, multi-view inference added Sep 2026. Pure-MLX port (lyonsno/pixal3d-mlx, no PyTorch, NATTEN replaced) benchmarked on an M4 Max 128 GB: ~10 min at res 512 (12 GB), ~21 min at res 1024 (33 GB, 4K texture).

demo_idea: beu: feed the beu label-overlay mock-up (front view) into pixal3d-mlx on the M4 Max at res 1024 and ship the GLB to a three.js viewer with a turntable and light rig; the client can read their own label on the 3D bottle, which TRELLIS.2/Hunyuan often blur. Lab post: Pixal3D vs TRELLIS.2 label legibility on the same inputs, with the M4 Max timing table.
mac_evidence: Upstream is CUDA-only: README Step 3 'NATTEN_CUDA_ARCH="xx" NATTEN_N_WORKERS=xx pip install natten==0.21.0 --no-build-isolation', flash_attn with 'ATTN_BACKEND=sdpa' fallback, TRELLIS.2 install (nvdiffrast, o_voxel, flex_gemm); no MPS/Apple mention. The pure-MLX port lyonsno/pixal3d-mlx (verified: trellmlx/ package present, pyproject deps mlx>=0.30 + numpy, no torch; MIT LICENSE) reports verbatim 'Performance (M4 Max, 128 GB)': '512 (FP16) | ~6K | ~10 min | ~12 GB | 2048', '512 (INT4) | ~12 min', '1024 (FP16) | ~15-26K | ~21 min | ~33 GB | 4096'; 'Resolution 512 fits comfortably in 16 GB unified memory. Resolution 1024 requires 64 GB'; 'No SDPA cliff — MLX Flash Attention handles 26K+ tokens where PyTorch MPS silently breaks at 18K'. Caveats driving the conservative call: 10–21 min per asset on the top-end M4 Max (offline batch only, never interactive); port is 1 star / 1 fork, single maintainer, last push 2026-07-05, and has no multi-view path (upstream added it 2026-09-01); appautomaton/mlx-spatial marks Pixal3D '🚧 In development' ('remains an in-development pipeline even when it writes a valid GLB'). No mlx-community port (search returned []), sebastianffx/Pixal3D-MLX on HF contains only .gitattributes; no ONNX/Transformers.js port (search returned []), so browser is out.
notes: Candidate is accurate on the core claims (pixel-aligned back-projection, TRELLIS.2 backbone on main branch, 1536 standard / 1024 low-VRAM, MIT, DINOv3 gating, MLX port with the quoted M4 Max numbers). Corrections: (1) param count is ~5.2B in DiTs (four, not three) — the shape cascade runs both a 512 and a 1024 img2shape model; (2) multi-view is upstream-only — the MLX port predates it, so a beu multi-shot workflow on Mac would require porting the *_mv weights yourself; (3) the mlx-spatial source is not a second working Mac path yet. Also exists: 'paper' branch = original Direct3D-S2 implementation (TencentARC/Pixal3D-D on HF, created 2026-05-01, dense/sparse512/sparse1024 folders); lyonsno's README credits pawel-mazurkiewicz/Pixal3D-mac (PyTorch MPS + Metal kernels) as the first Mac port — not verified here. HF Space TencentARC/Pixal3D is RUNNING on zero-a10g, so the label-legibility premise for beu can be sanity-checked in the browser before committing to a 24 GB download + DINOv3 access request. The 'front of the bottle is essentially the photo' claim is the paper's thesis, not something I could verify on a bottle/label input.

name: PosterOmni v1 (CVPR 2026)
domain: poster / label layout generation and editing
license: Weights: Apache-2.0 (HF cardData.license = apache-2.0 on MeiGen-AI/PosterOmni_v1). Code: NO license — GitHub API license=null, repo root has no LICENSE file (README.md, asset/, gradio_inference_showcase.py, images/, posteromni_inference.py, requirements.txt, run_6tasks_inference.sh, run_gradio_show.sh), README never mentions a license. Base Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit-2511: apache-2.0 (confirmed via HF API).
params: 20,430,401,088 BF16 per HF safetensors metadata (transformer only: QwenImageTransformer2DModel, 60 layers, 24 heads x 128 dim, 5 shards, ~41 GB bf16). Running it additionally needs the base pipeline's Qwen2.5-VL-7B text encoder + VAE from Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 (~15 GB bf16 more).
released: 2026-02 — arXiv 2602.12127 published 2026-02-12; GitHub first commit 2026-02-13; HF model repo created 2026-02-14; last GitHub push and HF lastModified both 2026-02-22 (nothing since; 234 HF downloads, 10 likes, 213 GitHub stars, 1 issue total).
what: Unified image-to-poster model (fine-tuned Qwen-Image-Edit transformer, Meituan + HKUST) covering six tasks: poster rescaling to a new aspect ratio, filling, extending, identity-driven, layout-driven (copy the layout of a reference poster with new content and given text strings) and style-driven creation, trained with task distillation plus a unified reward that scores text fidelity and visual consistency. Gradio demo and diffusers-compatible weights (transformer-only) released Feb 2026.
why_cool: Give it one product shot and it returns a finished campaign poster in 1:1, 9:16 and 16:9 with legible headline copy, or re-lays out an existing poster with new text - exactly the 'label/packaging layout' problem, from the PosterCraft (ICLR 2026) team. Apache-2.0 unlike the FLUX-dev-based PosterCraft.
demo_idea: beu: 'one shot, every format' - render a bottle with the current label design, then run poster_rescaling + poster_extending to produce Instagram 1:1, Story 9:16 and banner 16:9 variants carrying the brand copy, and poster_layout_driven_generation with a competitor's shelf poster as the layout reference. Runs with diffusers on MPS (QwenImageEditPlusPipeline, 40 steps; 20B bf16 fits in unified memory but expect many minutes per image) - queue it overnight and present a gallery. mflux already runs Qwen-Image/Qwen-Image-Edit natively on MLX, so swapping in the PosterOmni transformer weights is a promising lab task for fast Mac inference.
mac_evidence: No MLX/CoreML/MPS/Apple mention anywhere in the GitHub README or HF card (grep returned nothing). No MLX port: `api/models?author=mlx-community&search=PosterOmni` -> []; no ONNX/Transformers.js port: `search=PosterOmni onnx` -> []. Not GPU-only: requirements.txt lists only torch/torchvision/transformers/diffusers-from-source/opencv/gradio etc. — no flash-attn, xformers, triton or other CUDA-only kernels — and both posteromni_inference.py (line 248: `device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"`; line 52: `torch_dtype = torch.bfloat16 if device.startswith("cuda") else torch.float32`) and gradio_inference_showcase.py (lines 42-47) have an explicit CPU fallback. So out of the box on a Mac it silently runs the 20.4B transformer on CPU in fp32 (~82 GB transformer + ~28 GB text encoder fp32 — at the edge of 128 GB and extremely slow); a one-line patch to `device="mps"`, `torch.bfloat16` brings memory to ~56 GB total, which fits the M4 Max 128 GB unified memory, but the HF card's default recipe is `num_inference_steps=40, true_cfg_scale=4.0` (true CFG = 2 forward passes/step) of a 20B MMDiT -> many minutes per image on MPS. MLX path is plausible but unrealized: mflux README lists 'Qwen Image ... 20B ... Large model (slower) ... Has edit capabilities' and its qwen README states 'The model uses Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit-2511' with `mflux-generate-qwen-edit`; mlx-community hosts qwen-image-edit-2511-8bit, and mlx-community/TeleStyleV2-Qwen-Image-Edit-2511-bf16 (created 2026-06-24) is a precedent of a different 2511 fine-tuned transformer repackaged as a full drop-in snapshot for MLX. PosterOmni's config.json `_name_or_path` ends in 'qwen-2511_student_distill_.../transformer', so it is the same architecture and could be repackaged the same way — but nobody has published that, so it is a lab task, not a download.
notes: Candidate claims largely check out: real CVPR 2026 paper (Meituan + HKUST-GZ, PosterCraft authors), 6 tasks as described, transformer-only diffusers weights, 20.4B matches HF exactly. Corrections/caveats: (1) 'Apache-2.0' is true only for the weights — the GitHub inference/gradio code has no license at all, so treat the code as all-rights-reserved and rewrite your own loader (trivial: it is ~15 lines of QwenImageEditPlusPipeline + transformer swap). (2) Documentation is sloppy: the HF card tells you to load base `Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit-Plus`, which does not exist (HF API 401); README uses a local placeholder path 'Qwen-Image-Edit'; the real base per config.json is Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 (Dec 2025, apache-2.0, ~58 GB full download per mflux). README also points to a nonexistent `demo_gradio.py` (actual file gradio_inference_showcase.py) and the dataset badge is still 'TODO' — the single GitHub issue (#1, open since 2026-03-12) asks for the dataset with no reply. (3) Project looks abandoned post-release: last commit 2026-02-22, 1 issue, 234 HF downloads — there is no community of Mac users to lean on. (4) Realistic beu plan: patch to MPS bf16 and run 40-step true-CFG jobs overnight as the candidate suggests, or the more rewarding sml-lab task: fuse/repackage the PosterOmni transformer into an mflux-compatible 2511 snapshot (following the mlx-community TeleStyleV2-Qwen-Image-Edit-2511-bf16 layout) and optionally add the QIE-2511-Lightning 4-step LoRA to cut per-image time by ~10x — untested, but architecture-compatible. Nothing here runs in a browser; no Transformers.js/ONNX path for a 20B MMDiT.

BUT zero Mac evidence: README/HF card never mention MLX/CoreML/MPS/Apple, 0 GitHub issues mention mac/mps/apple/metal, README's install line is onnxruntime-gpu (not installable on macOS).
